It supports artistic work that breaks with traditional genres or is hard to define, and it may be assessed by more than one committee if relevant. Applicants are guided on whether to submit one application or split a project into separate subprojects across different funding programmes.
calls.project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.
When you break down your project into several applications, it is important that you also split up your budget, since you are not able to get the same expenses covered by more than one funding programme.
Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.
In some cases, two or more committees join together to fund a grant.
This will often happen, if a project’s budget is too large for one committee to fund it all.

calls.title: Art Media
calls.description: The Art Media grant supports written and/or spoken word publications that stimulate engagement with and discourse on contemporary visual art. It is aimed at projects such as article series, long reads and podcasts published on public media or online platforms. The grant can support individual practitioners or organisations working in this field, with the amount determined per application based on the budget.
calls.project_requirements: For written and/or spoken word publications. Applications can be submitted for e.g. a series of articles, long reads and podcasts that are published in/on (online) magazines, newspapers, social media channels or other online platforms. The planned publication must be accessible on at least one public medium or platform with appropriate reach. The project may not be directly linked to the applicant’s existing activities (e.g. an article or publication accompanying an exhibition). It is not possible to apply for a grant for television or film productions. It is not possible to apply for a grant for making profiles or portraits of artists.

calls.title: Apply for residency
calls.description: This is a residency opportunity at the Danish Art Workshops for professional artists, designers, craftspeople and art restorers who need access to large-format workshops and facilities. It offers studio and workshop access, accommodation in a guest flat, and consultation, with projects in either development/research or production/completion. Residencies can support work for exhibition, decoration, or other cultural activity in Denmark.
calls.project_requirements:
• DEVELOPMENT Projects deriving from material based, artistic development / research including material research, prototype production or other kinds of “work in process”.
• Projects that resemble research, exploration, and innovation.
• The purpose of the project must be well described.
• PRODUCTION Projects, that focus on production and completion of works for exhibition, decoration etc.
• It may be single works or a full exhibition.
• Projects targeted a public review in- or outside of Denmark.
• You can apply for a residency of up to six months.
• The length of the residency has to fit your project.
• Please state if you are flexible on the exact period of time or the studio you have applied for.
• In some cases, the committee assesses that a project can be done in a shorter period of time and this might result in a shorter term of residency, than was applied for.

calls.title: Call for individual mobility
calls.organisation: Culture Moves Europe / European Commission / Goethe-Institut
calls.description: This call supports individual mobility projects for artists and cultural professionals in another Creative Europe country. It offers a daily allowance, travel support, and possible top-ups for green mobility, family, visa, and accessibility needs. Applicants choose an international partner and carry out a project that follows two of the objectives: learn, create, explore, or connect.
calls.project_requirements: One project One artistic or cultural project to be carried out in another Creative Europe country, with the support of an international partner. This project must follow 2 of the following objectives: to learn, to create, to explore, or to connect. One international partner The international partner collaborates with the artists and cultural professionals during the project implementation. Applicants chose their own international partner, which can be an individual or an organisation.

calls.title: Artist Basic
calls.description: Artist Basic is a grant for visual artists to support the development of their professional practice and the creation of new work. It offers funding that can be used for research, experimentation, materials or equipment, commissions, and participation in exhibitions or events. The grant is intended to help artists expand their oeuvre, visibility, and cultural entrepreneurship.
calls.project_requirements:
For creating work.
That can include research, experimentation, or the purchase of new materials or equipment. Or it can help with the execution of a commission and/or participation in exhibitions or events in the Netherlands or abroad.

calls.title: Visual art – production and dissemination – exhibition venues
calls.description: Grants to produce and disseminate visual art.

calls.title: Application form – studio at Konstepidemin
calls.description: Konstepidemin is accepting applications for a studio space at its art center in Gothenburg. The form asks applicants to indicate their preferred studio size and area of interest, and it also notes community duties connected to being an artist at Konstepidemin. Applicants must submit a CV and a personal letter describing their practice and why they want a studio there.
calls.project_requirements: As an artist at Konstepidemin you are required to take part in the board, the culture committee, or one of our work sections: gallery, studio, stage, kids and youths, the international group, outdoor/gardening. Check area of interest (more than one is allowed).

calls.title: BUAT Curatorial Award 2027
calls.description: An international curatorial selection programme for contemporary artists worldwide. One artist will be selected for a solo curated presentation at BUAT FINE ART in Barcelona, and ten artists will be included on the Official Shortlist. The award also offers publication and recognition through the gallery’s curatorial programme.
calls.project_requirements: Rather than focusing on a single work, the Award considers each artist’s broader practice, with attention to conceptual clarity, artistic consistency and the coherence of the submitted body of work.

calls.title: Open Call: Abstract – Exhibition, Magazine Feature, Artist Interview
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit work for a virtual exhibition themed around abstraction. Selected artists may also be featured in the magazine and interviewed, with additional promotion through the organisation’s channels. Prizes include a solo show for first prize and a spot in a future group exhibition for second prize.
calls.project_requirements: The Goddessarts Magazine is excited to announce our upcoming theme: Abstract – a celebration of form, color, movement, and emotion. This exhibition invites artists to explore abstraction in all its powerful forms: gestural brushstrokes, geometric clarity, texture-driven work, conceptual abstraction, emotional expression, and beyond. Whether rooted in chaos or calm, minimalism or maximalism, we want to see how abstraction flows through your creative practice. All mediums and styles except video are welcome & everyone is encouraged to apply.

calls.title: Call for 2027 curatorial research fellowship
calls.description: This is a curatorial research grant for exhibition curators working on an original project related to image or photography. It supports a two-phase process: an initial research phase, followed by possible production and presentation of the exhibition if approved. The grant offers financial support for research and, subject to validation, for producing the project.
calls.project_requirements:
The selected project will be carried out in two phases: • research phase focusing on an exhibition project. • project production – subject to approval.
• Once the project has been selected, the curator will receive a grant of 5,000 euros to cover their expenses and royalties.
• The curator will be given six months to carry out research, at the end of which they must submit a proposal to the artistic direction team of the Rencontres d’Arles.
• Following an artistic evaluation, the Rencontres d’Arles will determine whether or not the project is feasible and approve its presentation format (Phase 2).
• The curator commits to: – select the works that will form the body of the exhibition and determine the rights for their display and reproduction; – design and draft an introductory text for the selection of photographs; – be present during the festival’s opening week and take part in the guided tour of the exhibition.

calls.title: Apply for artist-in-residence
calls.description: Konstepidemin offers international guest studios for artists to live and work in Gothenburg. The residency includes a studio space, bedroom, kitchen and bathroom, and artists also get access to shared facilities such as a printer/scanner/copy machine and a graphics workshop. Applications are accepted throughout the year for stays of one to six months.
calls.project_requirements: Konstepidemin’s five guest studios can be rented for periods of one to six months, and a minimum of one month is required. Please plan ahead and make sure to apply with some flexibility regarding your desired dates for residency. Longer periods are prioritized.

calls.title: MA Performance Practices (Autumn 2027)
calls.description: Applications are open for entry into the MA Performance Practices master’s degree programme starting in Autumn 2027. The programme focuses on practice-as-research and brings together performance art, choreography, contemporary theatre, experimental dance, and visual art. It emphasizes critical inquiry, politics and ethics, and collaborative learning with peers, guests, and researchers.

calls.title: THE ARTIST PRIZE 2027
calls.description: An open call competition for artists to submit artworks for the BBA Artist Prize 2027. Selected artists can be included in a shortlist and show their work in an exhibition in Berlin, with prizes and online promotion awarded to winners. The call welcomes all mediums and all themes.
calls.project_requirements:
Submit up to 5 artworks - this entitles you to be eligible for the long and shortlist and show your art at our exclusive exhibition in Berlin.
All themes welcome -

calls.title: Royal Institute of Painters in Water Colours
calls.organisation: Royal Institute of Painters in Water Colours (RI)
calls.description: Artists are invited to submit work for selection for the RI 215th Exhibition at Mall Galleries. The call focuses on contemporary watercolour and water-based media painting and offers selected artists the chance to exhibit alongside RI members, sell their work, and compete for prizes and awards. The exhibition will feature over 400 works from around the world.
calls.project_requirements: Works must have been completed within the last three years. Works should not be larger than 240 cm high and 150 cm wide including the frame. The Selection Committee has the right to exclude paintings that are over this limit. All works must be an original creation by the artist. Acceptable media: Watercolour or water-soluble mediums including watercolour, watercolour pencil, acrylic, ink or gouache (excluding water-soluble oils) on any appropriate support. Please specify the type of support (for example paper, board, wood, parchment, etc) as well as the medium. All paintings must be well presented, and should be suitably framed (no metal or clips frames are permitted) and glazed with picture glass (except in special circumstances as below, or by prior arrangement with the RI). Glazing in perspex and other similar transparent acrylic materials may be accepted, but only on works arriving from abroad or large works in frames exceeding 100 cm on the longest side. All works submitted to the exhibition should be framed unless there is a genuine aesthetic or technica

statement:
I am a choreographer and dancer making contemporary dance pieces for stage and site-specific settings. My work explores the body in public space, touch, and collective movement, often with non-professional performers and communities. I develop pieces through long rehearsal periods and improvisation.

I am looking for dance residencies with studio space, production support for new choreographic work, and festivals or programmes that present contemporary dance and performance.

calls.title: 33rd International Studio Program of the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar OPEN CALL 2026: On Absence
calls.organisation: ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit project proposals for the 33rd International Studio Program in Weimar. The 2026 theme is “On Absence,” and selected artists will take part in an international studio program connected to the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar.
calls.project_requirements: submit proposals for projects that explore absence and the absent through art, rethink absence in radically new ways, challenge it aesthetically, or use it as a tool for social critique.

calls.title: Creative Steps for Individuals
calls.description: Creative Steps for Individuals is a funding opportunity for artists and creative professionals in Wales who have experienced barriers to careers within the arts. It supports professional, business and organisational development rather than the creation of new work. Applicants can use the grant for activities such as mentoring, training, networking, business development, website development, or setting up a new organisation.
calls.project_requirements: Creative Steps for Individuals is for supporting career development, and NOT for creating new work or project delivery. Please bear in mind that you need to allow a minimum of 12 working weeks between the deadline date and the start date of your project. We cannot fund proposals that are already happening so we won’t accept your application if your proposal’s start date will come before we’ve had the opportunity to assess your application.

calls.title: OPEN CALL FOR PROJECTS LAB 4 WEIRD FUTURES
calls.description: Medialab Matadero is seeking proposals for the Collaborative Prototyping Lab, a creative residency within the year-long LAB 4 Weird Futures programme. Selected projects will be developed collaboratively during an intensive two-week lab in Madrid with mentors and collaborators, and presented at the OpenLAB festival.
calls.project_requirements: The primary activity of each LAB consists of a Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory: an intensive two-week Laboratory to collaboratively develop 5 experimental projects related to the themes that the LAB 4 addresses. Proposals submitted to this call must necessarily be open to the participation of collaborators interested in participating in their development. The Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory will take place from Monday to Friday between November 12th and 26th, 2025, both included, at Medialab's facilities in Matadero Madrid. The public presentation of the developed projects will be between November 27th and 29th, 2025, at the OpenLAB public event. Participation in the lab sessions must be in person and for the entire duration of the programme.

calls.title: Apply for artist-in-residence
calls.description: Konstepidemin offers international guest studios for artists to live and work in Gothenburg. The residency includes a studio space, bedroom, kitchen and bathroom, and artists also get access to shared facilities such as a printer/scanner/copy machine and a graphics workshop. Applications are accepted throughout the year for stays of one to six months.
calls.project_requirements: Konstepidemin’s five guest studios can be rented for periods of one to six months, and a minimum of one month is required. Please plan ahead and make sure to apply with some flexibility regarding your desired dates for residency. Longer periods are prioritized.

calls.title: OPEN STUDIOS 2027
calls.description: An open call inviting emerging choreographers to use the rehearsal spaces at Tanztendenz München from January 18 to 31, 2027. It offers a space to experiment, test new ideas, and exchange thoughts without the pressure of producing a finished work. Selected participants can also receive mentoring, rehearsal time, and support with travel, lodging, and finding accommodation.
calls.project_requirements:
From January 18 to 31, 2027, we are inviting emerging choreographers to use the rehearsal spaces at Tanztendenz München for the 15th time.
The goal of the Open Studios is not to develop a finished piece,but rather to begin testing out ideas and approaches.

calls.title: Performing arts – dance productions
calls.description: Grants for the artistic production and presentation of dance, both single projects and multi-year projects.

calls.title: Culture and Health
calls.organisation: Ministère de la Culture et ministère de la Santé
calls.description: This programme supports collaborative cultural projects in healthcare and medico-social settings. It is organized regionally and can take the form of artist residencies or other regional calls, bringing together cultural actors, artists, and health institutions to develop participatory artistic actions for patients, residents, families, and staff.
calls.project_requirements:
Projects must take place over a period between 1 June 2026 and 30 June 2027.
The Regional Directorate of Cultural Affairs, the Regional Health Agency and the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur Region are rolling out Culture and Health 2025 in the form of artist residencies for creation and transmission, promoting participatory artistic and cultural approaches led by artists.
This format of intervention makes it possible to present artistic proposals to audiences through residencies of at least six weeks (consecutive or not) within structures (hospital, nursing home, health centre, etc.). The approach includes creation periods and transmission periods with audiences.
All artistic fields are concerned: live performance (theatre, music, dance, circus, street art, etc.) visual arts, graphic arts, cinema, books and reading, museums, digital practices, etc.
The projects must be carried out during the 2026 calendar year.
Artistic and cultural projects co-built between three partners will be supported: at minimum a health establishment, a cultural facility and one or more qualified professional artists.
In order to help a larger number of establishments, projects allowing cooperation between several health establishments will be appreciated.
The actions must allow both:
• access to works,
• artistic practice,
• sharing around know-how,
• transmission of cultural knowledge.
Because of the audiences reached, and because time is needed to foster the encounter, the projects must provide for a minimum of 25 hours of artistic intervention with the participating people (excluding dissemination, preparation and meetings).
These projects may be multidisciplinary. They may propose actions in all artistic fields, books and reading, heritage, social sciences, architecture, scientific culture.
The following cannot be supported:
• animation projects and educational actions.
• art therapy workshops.
• artistic mediation with a relational purpose such as forum theatre or relational clowning.
• actions led by associations working in hospitals, whose very purpose is artistic intervention with hospitalised people.
• actions relating solely to communication, training or prevention objectives.
• projects consisting solely of programming performances, concerts, exhibitions.
• isolated initiatives designed by one department for one department.
• actions included in the institution’s operations.
• projects aimed solely at staff participation.
• public procurement procedures or the 1% artistic scheme.

calls.title: Open Call for Tokyo Wonder Site residency programs
calls.description: Tokyo Wonder Site Residency offers artist-in-residence programs for international creators in creative fields such as art, design, music and architecture. The page announces two residency programs for 2018: an International Creator Residency Program and a Research Residency Program. The residencies provide time and space for creation and research, along with opportunities to present work and exchange ideas.
calls.project_requirements:
• Residency Period: 3 months
• Residency Period: About 6 weeks

calls.title: Ink Still Wet 2027: Composer-Conductor Workshop with Steve Reich
calls.description: A fully funded composer-conductor workshop for composers and composition students. Selected participants develop a new orchestral work through workshops in New York City and Grafenegg, then rehearse and conduct the world premiere with the Tonkünstler Orchestra at the Grafenegg Festival. The programme is led by Steve Reich, with David Robertson as conducting coach.
calls.project_requirements:
Up to five selected composers will develop a new, unpublished and unperformed 5–7-minute orchestral work through two workshop phases in New York City and Grafenegg.
Applicants submit at least 2 minutes of a new, unpublished and unperformed orchestral work with a final duration of 5–7 minutes, together with a description of its concept or idea and the additional application materials specified in the full call.

calls.title: Application form – studio at Konstepidemin
calls.description: Konstepidemin is accepting applications for a studio space at its art center in Gothenburg. The form asks applicants to indicate their preferred studio size and area of interest, and it also notes community duties connected to being an artist at Konstepidemin. Applicants must submit a CV and a personal letter describing their practice and why they want a studio there.
calls.project_requirements: As an artist at Konstepidemin you are required to take part in the board, the culture committee, or one of our work sections: gallery, studio, stage, kids and youths, the international group, outdoor/gardening. Check area of interest (more than one is allowed).

calls.title: Open call: SummerLab with Dan Daw at P.A.R.T.S.
calls.description: This is a SummerLab curated during P.A.R.T.S.’ annual SummerSchool, led by choreographers Dan Daw and Sarah Blanc. It offers a week of movement, writing, conversation, and community exchange focused on inclusive dance practice and choreographic material inspired by Dan Daw Creative Projects’ work EXXY.
calls.project_requirements:
The workshop includes movement, writing, conversations and being together in a community.
A great willingness to listen and initiative to exchange are required.

calls.title: Residency Program 2027
calls.description: ada Studio is offering four residencies in 2027 for collaborative teams of two dance artists working in contemporary dance. The residencies are designed to support a research process and include studio use, artistic support, and a stipend for each resident.
calls.project_requirements:
The four five-week residencies are intended to support a research process.

A residency includes:
• Working at ada studio daily 10am – 4pm during the first 4 weeks of the residency
• 1 week for follow-up and writing the final report
• Opening of the working process (open rehearsal in the context of “reinkommen” at ada Studio on the fourth Friday of each residency (February 26/April 2/May 28/July 30, 2027)

Concept for a research project with a clear research question (Max. 3,000 characters)
Methodology of working on the question, in particular explanation of the collaborative working method (Max. 2,000 characters)
Preferred residency period (Residency #1 and/or #2 and/or #3 and/or #4; the more options the better!)

calls.title: Open call for artists
calls.description: This open call offers free support from digital dramaturges for artists or collectives interested in using technology in their artistic practice. It is meant for early-stage project development, short consultations, and conceptual questions about using digital and technological tools in artistic work.
calls.project_requirements:
• Early-stage project development or artist in need of a short consultation
• Conceptual questions around the use of technology
• Exploring how digital and technological tools can deepen your artistic approach
• This pilot-project runs until the end of the year 2026, which means that the consultations must also take place before the year ends.

calls.title: Seeking Support
calls.description: DGARTES presents open funding opportunities for artistic activity through its support programmes and funding lines. The page points applicants to the candidate support area and the management platform where application forms are available. It also links to the annual declaration listing the open calls and funding amounts for 2026.

calls.title: DancEUA Artist-in-Residence
calls.description: An international artist-in-residence programme for emerging dance artists from partner countries within the dancEUA project. It offers residencies in Sweden with studio access, mentorship, and a work-in-progress presentation for local audiences. The programme supports the development of new or ongoing dance and performing arts projects.
calls.project_requirements:
Each residency will host up to three dance projects, with one dance artist from Ukraine and two from other partner countries in each period.
The residencies welcome both solo and duet projects and give artists the chance to work with a professional mentor who will support them in developing their artistic creations.
The program culminates in a work-in-progress presentation, allowing artists to share their artistic works with the local audience of Tanum.

calls.title: Performing Arts – Competence Development and Publications
calls.description: Grants for competence development in the performing arts field, for example through workshops, publications, courses or conferences.

calls.title: Residencies 2027/28
calls.description: The Landis & Gyr Foundation offers artist residencies in Budapest, Bucharest, London, Sofia and Belgrade, as well as Zug residencies for writers and literary translators. The programme provides accommodation and a monthly stipend, and some locations also offer access to studio or rehearsal space. Applicants can choose one location and indicate preferred time periods.
calls.project_requirements: The desired time period (first and second preference) should also be stated.

calls.title: Performing Arts – Feasibility Project
calls.description: Grants for preliminary projects within performing arts that contribute to developing artistic concepts, methods and ideas, for example development of performing arts or choreography.

calls.title: Performing arts: International activities
calls.description: This grant programme supports international performing arts activities linked to performing arts in Denmark and Danish-produced performing arts abroad. It can fund guest performances, touring, site-specific performances, networking, research, workshops, residencies, and other activities that build international collaboration. Grants are available up to DKK 100,000.
calls.project_requirements:
The purpose of the program is to promote performing arts of high artistic quality in Denmark and Danish produced performing arts abroad. We achieve this by supporting internationalization such as:
• International guest performances touring and site specific performances, where an existing concept is adapted to the given context
• Networking and research aimed at long-term international collaborations and co-productions, including participation in workshops abroad as a speaker and the invitation of guests for performances in Denmark
• International residencies
The committee encourages you to incorporate your international activities in your long-term strategic planning, so that your international activities, if possible, are included in larger applications for the funding programme ‘Performing Arts for Children, Young People and Adults’, which has two annual deadlines in January and June. Here you can incorporate your international activities in applications for project grants or as part of your overall seasonal activities.

calls.title: Art Explora x Cité internationale des arts
calls.organisation: The Art Explora Foundation and the Cité internationale des arts
calls.description: A residency programme for French and international artists and researchers that supports projects engaging with contemporary issues such as new technologies, art and science, and environmental and social questions. It offers two formats: a SOLO programme for artists and a Collective programme for collectives, researchers, and curators. Residents receive studio space, a living allowance, a production grant, and travel to Paris.
calls.project_requirements: The programme invites candidates to propose a project that questions contemporary issues, including new technologies, the links between art and science, and environmental and social issues. Please explain why being based in France is necessary to the development of your project (conceptual, geographical and practical aspects, social ties, etc.).

calls.title: Kunsthaus am Wald International Artist in Residence Program Weitenhagen/ Germany
calls.description: This is an artist-in-residence program for the 2027 season at Kunsthaus am Wald in Weitenhagen, Germany. It invites artists from different disciplines and asks applicants to propose a project for the residency period and present their previous work. The location is remote, and site-specific projects are welcome but not required.
calls.project_requirements: Site-specific projects that engage with the spatial context are welcome, though they are not a mandatory requirement for a residency stay.

calls.title: Auditions Marta & Kim
calls.description: Marta & Kim are looking for experienced dancers and circus artists for their new performance FLUX (working title). The audition is for two additional performers who can work across contemporary dance and circus, with rehearsals in Rotterdam and a premiere in autumn 2025. Selected performers will join a process of 15 rehearsal weeks and touring.
calls.project_requirements: Rehearsals will start early next year 2025 with a premiere in the autumn. It is based on 15 rehearsal weeks, 4 days per week in Rotterdam.

calls.title: Temporarily Out of Place
calls.description: Treehouse NDSM is announcing an open call for its next exhibition, Temporarily Out of Place. The exhibition explores alternatives to current production systems and invites proposals that respond to large-scale challenges and contribute to alternative circular systems. Selected works may include performance, painting, making, installation, and video.
calls.project_requirements: Apply for the open call with a proposal that offers situated responses to large-scale challenges and contributes to the development of alternative circular systems. Submissions may span various media, including performance, painting, making, installation, and video.

calls.title: 2027 DancEUA Artist-in-Residence
calls.description: An international artist-in-residence opportunity for dance professionals within the DancEUA project. It offers residency time, studio access, mentoring, and a work-in-progress presentation in Sweden. The program is aimed at developing new work or further developing an existing dance or performing arts production.
calls.project_requirements:
looking to create a new work or further develop an existing dance or performing arts production.
Dance professionals working on solo or duet projects.
The program culminates in a work-in-progress presentation, allowing artists to share their artistic works with the local audience of Tanum.

calls.title: Research and Development
calls.description: Research and Development supports the development and creation of high-quality and ambitious work. It helps applicants explore new ideas and ways of working with partners, with funding available at two levels: small and large. The project should be aimed at reaching audiences and showing strong potential for future success.
calls.project_requirements:
Proposals should have a clear intention to create work that will reach audiences and demonstrate a strong potential for future success. Small Research & Development can explore how a new idea can become a developed product. It can give you time and space to pursue new concepts and take you beyond your usual creative practice. You should have partners committed to supporting your idea and show that their experience and involvement is appropriate at this stage. Be clear if you expect your work to be audience ready at the end of the term and if so, how you will ensure this. Consider how you’ll share your work in progress with the people and organisations you need onboard to take the project to realisation. Large Research & Development can be for development of works of larger scale or complexity or can build on a previous research and product development phase. If it is a first development stage, be clear on why a larger investment is necessary. Please include information on how the process will be shared and with who, for example details of any sharings and potential partners or stakeholders needed to support the work to its realisation. If this is a further development phase, it should lead to a product being ready to reach its audience. At this stage, you should have clear plans for presenting the work and should have developed audience and marketing plans. You can apply for a maximum of two research and development grants per work . You need to evidence why a further stage is needed and that it will be ‘audience ready’ at the end of this term. We accept Research and Development projects focussed on the artforms that we support . Your project will take place mostly in Wales , aiming to provide new and exciting experiences for audiences here. Your project must complement and enhance your usual programme of activity . This means it should not be part of your core activity or include core costs. This is particularly the case with Multi-Year Funded Organisations. Your project must involve working with others . The best projects happen when partners are involved. We’ll expect to see you working with at least one other individual or organisation who’ll support you to develop and deliver your project. This could be:
• a partner organisation
• artistic collaborator
• critical friend
• artistic mentor
Your partners can bring different skills and expertise to the proposal, to support you to realise your ambition for the work to be seen, to be relevant and reach its audience. Your project must be time limited . This means it has a definite start and end date. You must have other funding to contribute to the overall costs of your project . We can only support 90% of the project costs. At least 10% of your project income should come from a non-Arts Council or National Lottery source. This other funding can include Support in Kind, and there is no limit on Support in Kind. You must allow adequate lead in time . We’ll expect to see sufficient time built into your project to deliver the work effectively. This is particularly important when it comes to any audience development, outreach or sharing of work.

calls.title: International Studio Programme
calls.description: The International Studio Programme at Künstlerhaus Bethanien offers artists from around the world the chance to develop and deepen their artistic practice in Berlin. It provides individualized support, studio-based work, and opportunities to present work through open studios, studio visits, and exhibitions. The page also announces a Curatorial Fellow Program 2026 that brings selected curators, researchers, and artists into a year-long curatorial accompaniment within the residency program.

calls.title: EFFEA Call #5
calls.description: EFFEA Call #5 invites festivals and artists to apply for a residency programme. It supports collaborations between lead and partner festivals and an emerging artist, with the application requiring a proposed residency setup, motivation, and budget information.

calls.title: MA Performance Practices (Autumn 2027)
calls.description: Applications are open for entry into the MA Performance Practices master’s degree programme starting in Autumn 2027. The programme focuses on practice-as-research and brings together performance art, choreography, contemporary theatre, experimental dance, and visual art. It emphasizes critical inquiry, politics and ethics, and collaborative learning with peers, guests, and researchers.

statement:
I am a documentary filmmaker. I make creative documentaries and essay films about migration, labour and borders in Europe, shot over long periods with the people they portray. I direct, shoot and edit my own films, which are shown at film festivals and in cinemas.

I am looking for development and production funding for documentary film, film labs and pitching forums, and residencies for filmmakers to write and edit my next feature documentary.

calls.title: Different art forms
calls.description: This funding page explains how to apply when an artistic project combines different art forms or does not fit neatly into one category. It supports artistic work that breaks with traditional genres or is hard to define, and it may be assessed by more than one committee if relevant. Applicants are guided on whether to submit one application or split a project into separate subprojects across different funding programmes.
calls.project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.
When you break down your project into several applications, it is important that you also split up your budget, since you are not able to get the same expenses covered by more than one funding programme.
Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.
In some cases, two or more committees join together to fund a grant.
This will often happen, if a project’s budget is too large for one committee to fund it all.

calls.title: Call for submissions: Milan Machinima Festival MMXXVII
calls.description: The Milan Machinima Festival is inviting submissions for its 2027 edition, focused on machinima and game-based moving-image works. Selected works will be presented at the festival in Milan, with an international jury awarding a Critics’ Choice Award. The call emphasizes experimental, critical, and formally inventive uses of game technologies and virtual environments.
calls.project_requirements:
We invite artists, filmmakers, and experimental creators to submit machinima and game-based moving-image works that challenge convention, test the possibilities of digital form, and reflect on the cultural, political, and aesthetic conditions of life in computational worlds.
We are especially interested in works that adopt a critical or exploratory approach to game engines, gameplay footage, mods, assets, and simulated environments.
CGI-only animations will not be considered.
Selected works will be presented as part of the tenth edition of the Milan Machinima Festival opening on March 14, 2027.
If selected, we ask that the machinima not be screened elsewhere — including on personal websites or video-sharing platforms — for the duration of the festival.

calls.title: Elisabeth-Büttner Fellowship for Film Culture
calls.organisation: Bundesministerium für Wohnen, Kunst, Kultur, Medien und Sport
calls.description: A stipend for projects in film culture, including film preservation, film heritage, film programming and curatorship. It supports work that contributes to Austrian film culture and can take place in Austria or abroad, often in connection with a film-cultural institution. The stipend is awarded for up to six months and includes monthly funding.
calls.project_requirements: Applications may be submitted for projects in the fields of Film Preservation, Film Heritage, Film Programming and Curatorship that contribute to Austrian film culture, require a well-founded engagement with Austrian film history (film/history/Austria) and theories of film, and aim at a revision of images. The projects may take place in Austria and abroad and be connected to a film-cultural institution (archives, cinemas, film festivals, etc.). Projects in the field of artistic research are expressly welcome. Permissible activities: in particular work and study residencies, (artistic) research, development of program series, workshops, exhibitions, publications and film mediation offerings, et al. Duration: max. 6 months

calls.title: Film Submission for 39 FILMFEST DRESDEN 2027
calls.description: FILMFEST DRESDEN is inviting filmmakers to submit short films for its 39th edition in 2027. The call covers competition entries and official selection programmes, including special sections such as Kids, Youth, Panorama, Experiments, and Open Air. Selected films will be screened at the festival in Dresden.
calls.project_requirements:
Please make sure that your submission includes English subtitles if the original language is not English. This also applies to German-language productions.
When submitting your entry, please upload both a video file with English subtitles burned into the video and a subtitle file (format: SRT, STL, or XML).
Works-in-progress are eligible for entry if submitted by the deadline. The cut you submit should at least be picture locked. Please label your submission "work-in-progress” for example in the opening credits or the synopsis and specify what is incomplete and still to be finished (final sound mixes, colour correction or completed visual effects).
Re-submissions are not accepted !
Please note that, if your film is selected, only films on 35mm or DCP will be accepted for festival screenings!

calls.title: Open call for an audiovisual residency with focus on short documentary film
calls.organisation: The Goethe-Institut and Bozar – Centre for Fine Arts Brussels together with Atelier Graphoui, Cinemaximiliaan and Sound Image Culture - SIC
calls.description: This is an audiovisual residency programme in Brussels for four emerging professional filmmakers. The selected residents will meet, exchange ideas, and produce individually a short documentary film in Belgium during 2022. The programme is part of Halaqat and includes collective feedback days and masterclasses.
calls.project_requirements: produce individually a short documentary film in Belgium during 2022. Amongst the four chosen residents, two residents will be connected to Cinemaximiliaan and two will be connected to Atelier Graphoui, according to their profile and project. All four residents will have two collective feedback-days with SIC and can take part in its masterclasses. The residency aims to focus on the development and realisation of hybrid films (preferably single screen) in an artistic and experimental way

calls.title: Support for Creative Travel in the Film Arts Sector
calls.description: This is a funding call in the film arts field. It supports creative trips and related activities through the VKKF project competition system. The page links to the programme rules and the application system.

calls.title: AIR - Residencies Abroad 2027 for Visual Artists, Media Artists and Filmmakers
calls.description: This call offers international working residencies in 2027 for visual artists, media artists, and filmmakers. Selected artists can spend time at partner institutions in several countries, with accommodation and/or studio access provided at each destination and a stipend from the City of Salzburg. The programme is intended to support artistic work, exchange, and the development of future projects and collaborations.
calls.project_requirements: At the end of the stay, a written work report including image material must be submitted to the City of Salzburg without being requested. The report should comprehensively present the artistic activities on site and convey to what extent this working stay was relevant for future artistic projects and collaborations and describe them. Works, exhibitions, etc. should be presented in the report using image material.

calls.title: Experimenta Associates. early-career curatorial mentorships
calls.description: This is an open call for two early-career curators to join Experimenta at the BFI London Film Festival as Associates. The selected applicants will be mentored by the Experimenta programmers and LFF teams while engaging with artists’ moving image, and may also publish a contextual piece on the BFI or LUX website. The role includes viewing, discussion, social media engagement, and live-event/Q&A support during the festival.
calls.project_requirements: Please note that the majority of viewing in this role will take place between 20 June and the 15 July.

calls.title: Creation of content for the programme “LATVIJAS SKOLAS SOMA”
calls.description: This is a funding call for creating content for the Latvian School Bag programme. It supports projects that develop cultural content for use in the programme and is run as a targeted programme competition by the State Culture Capital Foundation. The page links to the competition rules and application system.

calls.title: Call for Entries
calls.description: art+film+vienna is inviting submissions for its fourth festival edition in May 2027 at the Breitenseer Lichtspiele. The call is for experimental moving-image projects that can include film, video, performative, spatial, installation-based, interactive, or live elements. The festival focuses on work that crosses film, visual art, performance, sound, and digital media.
calls.project_requirements: In addition to single-channel film and video works, submissions may incorporate performative, spatial, installation-based, interactive, or live elements.

calls.title: Basic - Writing
calls.description: This is a funding programme for the writing stage of feature-length fiction, documentary, and animation projects. It supports script development and writing, with funding amounts varying by project type and role, and requires delivery of the first script draft or a treatment/script outline.
calls.project_requirements:
Projects included in the program are fiction, documentary and animation projects, feature-length, with a minimum duration of 70 minutes.
The purpose of this funding stage is the development and writing of a feature-length screenplay for a fiction film, or an analytical screenplay plan/treatment for a documentary film.
Upon completion of this funding stage, the screenwriter delivers the first draft of the screenplay.
Upon completion of this funding stage, the screenwriter delivers a treatment/screenplay plan of at least 2,500 words.
The contracting party is obliged to deliver the artistic deliverables and the financial report within 12 months from the signing of the agreement.

calls.title: French cultural network residencies around the world
calls.description: This page presents the residency programmes run by the French cultural network abroad. It explains that these residencies support artistic research, experimentation, and professional networking across many creative fields. The page also points to current calls for applications and provides access to the network’s residency map and charter.
calls.project_requirements: A residency is defined by all of the following characteristics: 1. The provision of accommodation and a workspace for the artist. 2. A minimum duration of one month, essential to understanding the local context and to establishing lasting contacts that are relevant to the project, whilst at the same time limiting the residency’s impact on the environment. 3. Administrative, technical, professional and artistic support to encourage research development. 4. A minimum of 70% of the residency time is devoted to the artist's project. 5. The awarding of a residency grant to the artist. Residencies organised within France's cultural network abroad are primarily residencies focusing on creation, research or experimentation. They are not intended to support programmes that are first and foremost geared towards distribution or circulation (touring exhibitions, setting up of exhibitions, participation in symposiums, etc.) or towards training or continuing education, nor are they intended to respond to artistic commissions. Residencies may, however, go hand in hand with other objectives of the post.

calls.title: Production of low-budget feature-length fiction films and fiction short films
calls.description: This is a funding call for the production of low-budget feature-length fiction films and fiction short films. It is part of VKKF’s regular project competitions and is submitted through the VKKF project application system. The call supports film projects in the film arts field.

calls.title: Production of low-budget feature fiction films and fiction short fiction films
calls.description: This is a funding call for the production of low-budget feature fiction films and fiction short films. It is part of VKKF’s regular project competitions and is submitted through the VKKF project application system. The page points to a separate regulation document for the full rules.

calls.title: INTERNATIONAL OPEN CALL 2027
calls.description: Velferden is offering self-directed residencies in Sokndal, south western Norway, between February 1st and June 30th 2027. The residency provides a peaceful working environment in a mountainous and forested landscape shaped by mining activity, with access to a private studio, project rooms, and accommodation. It is aimed at artists, critical theorists, and researchers who want to develop their own work in a cross-disciplinary setting.
calls.project_requirements:
You can apply for a period of 1 - 3 months.
We don´t expect to see finished results, but we would like to hear about your process and practice in our monthly public event Velferden Presenting”.

calls.title: Support for Creative Travel in the Field of Film Arts
calls.description: This call supports creative travel in the field of film arts. It is a funding opportunity within VKKF’s regular project competitions and is administered through the fund’s project application system.

calls.title: Dhërmi Residency
calls.description: Dhërmi Residency is an artist residency in the Albanian Riviera that offers an inspiring setting for research, reflection, and creative production. It invites artists to develop new works in dialogue with place, memory, and landscape while engaging with the village’s cultural and natural heritage. The residency is focused on video art, moving image, experimental film, and contemporary media.

calls.title: Completed film
calls.description: This is a funding programme for completed films. It offers support or financing for feature-length films, and honorary support for short films that meet the programme’s conditions. Applications are submitted electronically through the E-services platform.
calls.project_requirements:
The program is addressed to producers of feature films, with a duration of at least 70’, which have not been financed or subsidized by the EKK at the production stage.
Eligible for evaluation are Greek production films that have not yet been screened or were screened for the 1st time (in a cinema theater and/or online) in the last 12 months (1/7 – 30/6) before the submission deadline.
Submissions of different versions of films (cut) are not accepted if their first version was screened prior to the aforementioned period.
The amount of the funding cannot exceed 50% of the final cost of the film, as will be certified by an Auditor’s report.
Within three (3) months from the posting of the results in DIAVGEIA, the producers must submit all necessary supporting documents for the signing of the agreement with the EKK.
Upon the expiry of this period, the approval automatically ceases to be valid and the EKK support/funding is canceled.
In this program, short fiction films, documentaries or animation films may be selected honorarily for support, which participate in an official festival program belonging to CATEGORY A, and have been produced without EKK funding.

calls.title: Research and Development
calls.description: Research and Development supports the development and creation of high-quality and ambitious work. It helps applicants explore new ideas and ways of working with partners, with funding available at two levels: small and large. The project should be aimed at reaching audiences and showing strong potential for future success.
calls.project_requirements:
Proposals should have a clear intention to create work that will reach audiences and demonstrate a strong potential for future success. Small Research & Development can explore how a new idea can become a developed product. It can give you time and space to pursue new concepts and take you beyond your usual creative practice. You should have partners committed to supporting your idea and show that their experience and involvement is appropriate at this stage. Be clear if you expect your work to be audience ready at the end of the term and if so, how you will ensure this. Consider how you’ll share your work in progress with the people and organisations you need onboard to take the project to realisation. Large Research & Development can be for development of works of larger scale or complexity or can build on a previous research and product development phase. If it is a first development stage, be clear on why a larger investment is necessary. Please include information on how the process will be shared and with who, for example details of any sharings and potential partners or stakeholders needed to support the work to its realisation. If this is a further development phase, it should lead to a product being ready to reach its audience. At this stage, you should have clear plans for presenting the work and should have developed audience and marketing plans. You can apply for a maximum of two research and development grants per work . You need to evidence why a further stage is needed and that it will be ‘audience ready’ at the end of this term. We accept Research and Development projects focussed on the artforms that we support . Your project will take place mostly in Wales , aiming to provide new and exciting experiences for audiences here. Your project must complement and enhance your usual programme of activity . This means it should not be part of your core activity or include core costs. This is particularly the case with Multi-Year Funded Organisations. Your project must involve working with others . The best projects happen when partners are involved. We’ll expect to see you working with at least one other individual or organisation who’ll support you to develop and deliver your project. This could be:
• a partner organisation
• artistic collaborator
• critical friend
• artistic mentor
Your partners can bring different skills and expertise to the proposal, to support you to realise your ambition for the work to be seen, to be relevant and reach its audience. Your project must be time limited . This means it has a definite start and end date. You must have other funding to contribute to the overall costs of your project . We can only support 90% of the project costs. At least 10% of your project income should come from a non-Arts Council or National Lottery source. This other funding can include Support in Kind, and there is no limit on Support in Kind. You must allow adequate lead in time . We’ll expect to see sufficient time built into your project to deliver the work effectively. This is particularly important when it comes to any audience development, outreach or sharing of work.

calls.title: Call for collaborators for the collaborative prototyping laboratory LAB 4 Weird Futures
calls.description: LAB 4 Weird Futures is a multidisciplinary research and collaborative production programme at Medialab Matadero Madrid. It includes a two-week prototyping laboratory, artistic projects, workshops, seminars and public events, and this call is for collaborators to take part in the development of selected projects. The programme culminates in the OpenLAB festival in November 2025.

calls.title: Free Camera
calls.description: Caméra libre is a residency programme in France for foreign filmmakers in difficult situations. It is organised by the CNC in partnership with the Cité internationale des arts and L’usage du monde au 21e siècle. The programme supports development and writing for feature-length cinema projects.
calls.project_requirements: Feature film

calls.title: Art Explora x Cité internationale des arts
calls.organisation: The Art Explora Foundation and the Cité internationale des arts
calls.description: A residency programme for French and international artists and researchers that supports projects engaging with contemporary issues such as new technologies, art and science, and environmental and social questions. It offers two formats: a SOLO programme for artists and a Collective programme for collectives, researchers, and curators. Residents receive studio space, a living allowance, a production grant, and travel to Paris.
calls.project_requirements: The programme invites candidates to propose a project that questions contemporary issues, including new technologies, the links between art and science, and environmental and social issues. Please explain why being based in France is necessary to the development of your project (conceptual, geographical and practical aspects, social ties, etc.).

calls.title: Co-production window
calls.description: A funding programme for the production of feature-length and short fiction, documentary, and animation films in co-production with foreign producers. It offers subsidy support for projects that can strengthen links between Greek and European audiovisual production and attract foreign investment to the Greek audiovisual industry.
calls.project_requirements:
Type | kind: feature-length, short film | fiction, documentary, animation (≥5’)
A project that has been submitted, or strengthened or rejected twice (i.e. definitively) in another Funding Program “Minority Co-production” of EKKOMEDE is not accepted.
A project that was rejected during its evaluation in this specific program may, after being improved, be submitted again for evaluation in the program, with a new application and for one (1) more time only.
A project that has been rejected by this program is excluded from the published on the EKKOMEDE website “Funding Programs for Film Projects and Works”.
Within the framework of this action, eligible are projects for the production of feature-length or short films: fiction documentary animation, of at least 5’ duration, which concern production and for which no work has started before the submission of a proposal/application for support in this Call.
Each project must be feasible and it must be possible to deliver the final cut within twelve (12) months from the signing of the relevant contract.
No extension of the delivery of the foreseen work (final cut) is provided.
The projects must have confirmed funding from a State funding body and/or from a television station in at least one of the co-production countries.

calls.title: CPH:DOX 2027
calls.description: CPH:DOX 2027 is open for submissions for films and for projects to CPH:FORUM and CPH:ROUGHCUT. Filmmakers can submit completed films, and project holders can submit projects for the forum and rough cut sections of the festival.

calls.title: European Festivals Fund for Emerging Artists – EFFEA
calls.description: EFFEA is an artist-in-residence programme that supports emerging artists through festivals across Europe. It offers selected artists time, space, support, and international visibility, while also fostering cross-border collaboration among festivals. The fund has two residency categories: Discovery and Springboard.
calls.project_requirements: The EFFEA Residency is an artist-in-residence programme aimed at fostering the international career of emerging artists in the seat of a minimum of 3 festivals . Co-produced by a leading festival in collaboration with partner festivals, each from a different eligible country , the residency provides emerging artists with dedicated time, space and support to explore their ideas and creative projects, whether original works or the evolution of existing ones .

calls.title: Short Film
calls.description: This is a funding programme for short films in fiction, documentary, and animation. It supports projects at the production stage and offers financial backing for eligible proposals. The programme is aimed at strengthening short-form filmmaking and supporting new creators.
calls.project_requirements:
Projects included in the program are short fiction, documentary and animation projects, with a duration of up to 40 minutes.
If the project receives pre-approval for funding, the creator must secure a producer within the validity period of the pre-approval.
Within this period, the producer must submit the final production file of the film.
If the final budget shows a negative deviation greater than 25% from the budget on the basis of which the pre-approval was granted, the pre-approval ceases to be valid.
Non-self-contained projects, interactive projects or projects concerning episodes of a series are not accepted.

calls.title: Call for Entries
calls.description: This is a call for current works for EMAF in the sections Film, Installation, and Expanded. Selected works can be shown in the festival program and exhibition, with fees/honoraria and invited participation at the festival.
calls.project_requirements: We invite submissions of current works in the sections Film (experimental films of any length and any thematic focus), Installation (installative, interactive, spatial or sculptural media art works) and Expanded (performances, live events or workshops). Submissions for the Installation section should relate to the 2027 festival theme, which will center on the archive – as an instrument of knowledge production, a site of critical intervention and a space for alternative visions of the future. Applications for the Installation and Expanded sections must include a detailed description, tech rider, cost calculation and visual material.

calls.title: Call for films & projects
calls.description: Visions du Réel is inviting submissions for its 58th edition, including films for the official selection and projects for VdR–Industry activities. The call covers several competition and industry sections for documentary works, with selected films screened at the festival in Nyon. It also includes project opportunities such as VdR–Pitching, Work in Progress, and Rough Cut Lab.
calls.project_requirements:
The films in competition are screened in world, international or European premiere.
Submissions of films only available for Swiss premiere will not be considered.
Projects are presented in VdR–Industry for the first time at their current stage.
Only films having their world, international, or European premiere are eligible.
Films must have at least a world, international, European, or Swiss premiere.

calls.title: Call for Film Projects: SIC 2027
calls.description: SoundImageCulture is a one-year program in Brussels that supports filmmakers, artists and thinkers in the development of a film project. Selected participants work with coaches, peers, international guests, masterclasses and seminars, and present their work publicly at the end of the cycle.
calls.project_requirements:
To be present at the collective sessions
To bring new materials (rushes, edits, try-outs) to every session
To hold at least one meeting (max. 2 hours) with your personal coach in between sessions
To give feedback and assistance to your peers

calls.title: Creative Steps for Individuals
calls.description: Creative Steps for Individuals is a funding opportunity for artists and creative professionals in Wales who have experienced barriers to careers within the arts. It supports professional, business and organisational development rather than the creation of new work. Applicants can use the grant for activities such as mentoring, training, networking, business development, website development, or setting up a new organisation.
calls.project_requirements: Creative Steps for Individuals is for supporting career development, and NOT for creating new work or project delivery. Please bear in mind that you need to allow a minimum of 12 working weeks between the deadline date and the start date of your project. We cannot fund proposals that are already happening so we won’t accept your application if your proposal’s start date will come before we’ve had the opportunity to assess your application.

calls.title: Gjon Mili Residency Program 2027 Call for Applications
calls.description: The Gjon Mili Residency Program invites artists to take part in a residency focused on video art, short film, documentary, and experimental moving-image practices. The program takes place in Dhërmi, Albania, and is connected to the Gjon Mili International Video Art Festival. Selected artists are expected to develop a project during the residency period.
calls.project_requirements: A short description of the project or idea the artist would like to develop during the residency, preferably connected to moving image, landscape, architecture, memory, public space, or experimental media practices.

statement:
I am a poet and translator. I write poetry and short prose, and translate contemporary poetry between Latvian and English. My books deal with language, family history and the Baltic landscape. I also perform my poems at readings and literary festivals.

I am looking for writing residencies, literary grants and translation grants, and opportunities to publish and present my work at literature festivals.

calls.title: Creative Development Promotion Scholarship Target Programme
calls.description: This programme offers creative development stipends through the Latvian State Culture Capital Foundation. It is a funding opportunity for artistic and cultural work across several disciplines, with applications submitted through the VKKF system.

calls.title: Support for the publication of books in Icelandic
calls.description: This is a funding scheme that provides temporary financial aid to publishers for the publication of books in Icelandic. It reimburses part of eligible publication costs, including labour, printing, translation, proofreading, and promotion. Applications are submitted electronically through the application system.
calls.project_requirements:
The published book must be in Icelandic.
Eligible expenses incurred in the publication of the book and for which the applicant requests support must amount to at least ISK 1 million. Lower thresholds for books published on digital media and for certain classes of books may be laid down in a Regulation.
Costs incurred in the publication of a book intended primarily as a means of promoting a particular product or service do not qualify as eligible expenses under this Act.

calls.title: Creation of content for the “LATVIAN SCHOOL BAG” programme
calls.description: This is a funding call for creating content for the Latvian School Bag programme. It supports projects connected to the programme’s educational and cultural content, with rules set out in the attached regulations. Applicants submit proposals through VKKF’s project application system.
calls.project_requirements: The goals, tasks, applicant group and other issues related to the course of the program competition are set out in the competition regulations of each target program.

calls.title: Public call for proposing public needs in culture of the Republic of Croatia for 2027
calls.organisation: Ministarstvo kulture i medija Republike Hrvatske
calls.description: This public call invites proposals for programs, projects, activities, and events in culture that are of interest to the Republic of Croatia. It covers a wide range of cultural fields, from museums and libraries to literature, performing arts, visual arts, heritage protection, and cultural infrastructure. Applications are submitted electronically through the ministry’s e-application forms.
calls.project_requirements:
in the following activities and areas:
• museum activities
• library activities
• monographs in the field of culture and art
• support for publishing books
• support for foreign publishers for publishing translations of works by Croatian authors
• publishing journals and periodic electronic publications
• literary events
• literary programs within bookselling activities
• dramatic and dance arts and performing arts
• music and music-stage arts
• visual arts
• interdisciplinary and new artistic and cultural practices
• cultural and artistic amateurism (music and folklore)
• international cultural cooperation
• regular activities of associations in culture
• construction, reconstruction and equipping of cultural infrastructure
• digitization of cultural heritage
• protection and preservation of terrestrial archaeological heritage
• protection and preservation of underwater archaeological heritage
• protection and preservation of immovable cultural property
• protection and preservation of movable cultural property
• protection and preservation of intangible cultural property.

calls.title: Circulation of European literary works
calls.organisation: Creative Europe Programme (CREA) / European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA)
calls.description: This call supports projects that translate, publish, distribute, and promote European works of fiction. It aims to increase the transnational circulation and diversity of European literary works, with particular emphasis on works written in less widely translated languages. It also encourages activities that support literary translators, reading promotion, and cooperation across the book value chain.
calls.project_requirements:
This action supports projects that translate, publish, distribute, and promote European works of fiction .
Proposals should address the following Call specific priorities: to increase the transnational circulation and the diversity of European literary works, through the translation, publication, distribution, and promotion of works of fiction, with particular emphasis on those written in less widely translated languages.
to promote reading and the linguistic and cultural diversity of European literature to a large audience.
to support the profession of literary translator, in line with the principles of good working conditions and fair remuneration publishers should ensure that the names of the translators appear visibly in published books, and preferably on the cover, and that the source language is clearly mentioned.
to increase the competitiveness of the book sector by encouraging cooperation between different actors within the book value chain, notably between publishers, booksellers, and libraries.
Activities that can be funded under the present call are translation, publication, promotion, and distribution activities as well as activities addressing the themes and priorities described above.

calls.title: Lifetime Stipend Programme
calls.description: This is a funding programme for lifetime stipends administered by the State Culture Capital Foundation of Latvia. It supports cultural workers through a dedicated stipend scheme and is presented as part of VKKF’s programme competitions. Applicants submit proposals through the VKKF project application system.

calls.title: Creation of content for the programme “LATVIJAS SKOLAS SOMA”
calls.description: This is a funding call for creating content for the Latvian School Bag programme. It supports projects that develop cultural content for use in the programme and is run as a targeted programme competition by the State Culture Capital Foundation. The page links to the competition rules and application system.

calls.title: Work Grant
calls.description: This is a work grant for translators that supports longer and more intensive work on a project, including research and revision. Applicants submit an online application and, if successful, upload supporting documents after receiving a confirmation email.
calls.project_requirements:
Source language
Author first name last name
Genre
Title / project
Publisher
Expected length
Submission deadline
Planned publication date
Required working time
Base fee
Print run participation
Subsidiary rights participation

calls.title: Art Residency Program
calls.description: Can Serrat offers an international art residency program for writers and contemporary artists from around the world. The program provides short- and medium-term residencies with time, space, follow-up, individual and collective support, and a professional network. Some calls include full grants and partial grants.
calls.project_requirements: There is no expectation of a finished product at the end of the residency, and the program does not aim to organize gallery exhibitions.

calls.title: Residencies 2027/28
calls.description: The Landis & Gyr Foundation offers artist residencies in Budapest, Bucharest, London, Sofia and Belgrade, as well as Zug residencies for writers and literary translators. The programme provides accommodation and a monthly stipend, and some locations also offer access to studio or rehearsal space. Applicants can choose one location and indicate preferred time periods.
calls.project_requirements: The desired time period (first and second preference) should also be stated.

calls.title: Public Call for Funding Sample Translations of Works by Croatian Authors into Foreign Languages in 2026
calls.organisation: Ministarstvo kulture i medija Republike Hrvatske
calls.description: This call supports sample translations of works by Croatian authors into foreign languages. It aims to promote Croatian literature and non-literary works abroad and strengthen literary mediation and rights sales. The Ministry funds translator fees and, if requested, printing costs for a promotional booklet.
calls.project_requirements: The sample translation submitted to the Public Call must be the first translation of the original literary or non-literary work written in the Croatian language into a specific foreign language. Sample translations into English are preferred, but other languages with strong promotional potential are also acceptable. One applicant may request support for at least 10 and at most 20 sample translations, with no more than 3 translations of a single work by the same author. Each application must contain proposals for translating sample translations of works by at least 3 different Croatian authors. The sample translation must comprise at least 15 and at most 30 author’s sheets of prose text, or at least 5 and at most 10 poems (from 75 to 150 verses). An agreement will be concluded with the beneficiary of the funds, regulating the obligations of the beneficiary and the Ministry of Culture and Media. The beneficiary of the funds for financing sample translations through this Public Call is obliged to allow the publication of the financed sample translations on the website https://www.croatian-literature.hr/ without any compensation for the Ministry of Culture and Media and to enable the Ministry to use the co-financed sample translations for promotional purposes without any compensation. The beneficiary is obliged, no later than 1 December of the current year, to submit a complete financial report with evidence of the executed transactions, the co-financed sample translations in printed and electronic form, as well as 10 copies of the promotional booklet if funds for printing have been approved.

calls.title: Different art forms
calls.description: This funding page explains how to apply when an artistic project combines different art forms or does not fit neatly into one category. It supports artistic work that breaks with traditional genres or is hard to define, and it may be assessed by more than one committee if relevant. Applicants are guided on whether to submit one application or split a project into separate subprojects across different funding programmes.
calls.project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.
When you break down your project into several applications, it is important that you also split up your budget, since you are not able to get the same expenses covered by more than one funding programme.
Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.
In some cases, two or more committees join together to fund a grant.
This will often happen, if a project’s budget is too large for one committee to fund it all.
