calls.title: ENTER
calls.description: ENTER is the Nordic Culture Fund’s programme for ambitious ideas that can open up new perspectives and set new things in motion through collaboration. It supports initiatives that want space to experiment, learn as they go, and test new directions before the outcome is fully clear. The programme offers funding for projects with a Nordic connection and a strong role for arts and culture.
calls.project_requirements: To be eligible for funding through ENTER, your initiative must have a Nordic anchoring and be built on collaboration across borders. Arts and culture must be a significant part of the initiative, but we also encourage collaborations with other sectors, practices and areas of society. ENTER does not support initiatives whose primary purpose is: education or study visits participation in conferences, festivals, events or similar activities tours or travelling exhibitions productions or publications organisational running costs or core funding construction projects or the purchase of technical equipment for day-to-day operations You can only apply for activities that take place after you have received the funding decision from the Nordic Culture Fund. Your initiative must be completed and reported on no later than one year after the stated start date. As a general rule, the project periods for ENTER cannot be extended.

calls.title: Auditions Conversations – New XRPerformance by Paul Boereboom & Leon Rogissart
calls.description: Conversations is a new music theatre production that combines live performance, music, movement, and XR technology. The call is for classical vocal performers to join an international creative process for an immersive, participatory performance. Selected performers will take part in paid rehearsals and performances in Rotterdam.
calls.project_requirements:
An immersive music theatre ritual for an intimate audience of 80 participants.
In a shared space, performers and audience move together through a collective experience of music, reflection, and encounter.
The performance is participatory and interactive.
As a performer, you engage directly with the audience: you are not playing a character, but performing as yourself.
Presence, attentiveness, and openness towards the participants are central to the work.
The project explores themes of inner dialogue, presence, and collective ritual, and uses technology as a supportive dramaturgical layer rather than a dominant element.

calls.title: Touring and activity grants for musicians, artists, ensembles and bands
calls.description: This funding scheme supports concert and touring activity in Norway and abroad for professional musicians, artists, ensembles and bands across all genres. It offers project grants or operating grants for concert production, touring, development and ongoing activity. The scheme especially emphasizes concerts in Norway and aims to give audiences access to a wide range of concerts.
calls.project_requirements:
Project grants for specific concerts and tours. We provide grants for individual tours or for several concerts or tours over the course of a year. If you are applying for project grants, you can apply for project grants at all three application deadlines of the scheme all concert- and tour-related expenses may be included in the application, including expenses for necessary rehearsals or necessary pre-production and administration related to the concerts the project period must be a maximum of one year

Operating grants

By operating grants we mean grants that are included in the overall annual financing of an activity or a regular activity. This means that you must apply for the entire calendar year and describe the overall concert and tour activity, development and operations throughout the year in the application. To apply for operating grants, you must be an activity with an organization number or have a regular activity with its own name and budget, which is part of a larger activity for a minimum of three years have had extensive concert activity throughout the year and/or be a larger ensemble or band that has had year-round operations for a minimum of three years You can apply for grants for up to three years, and we encourage you to apply for multi-year grants. Please note that you can only apply at the September application deadline. Please also note that the committee may award a different type of grant than the one you applied for.

calls.title: Master stipend for diversity knowledge
calls.description: This is a master stipend for students developing new knowledge about equality and diversity in the arts and culture sector. It supports master projects on diversity in art and culture, with funding that can cover travel, literature, seminars, and other necessary project costs.

Projects that fall outside the purpose of the scheme or the framework of the Norwegian Directorate for Culture’s coordinator assignment cannot receive support. In the application, you must also confirm that you will participate in a joint working seminar for scholarship recipients. Note that the seminar will take place in the Norwegian Directorate for Culture’s premises in Oslo. If you have a long travel distance, the Norwegian Directorate for Culture will cover travel costs.

The fellowship is aimed at supporting conductors from backgrounds currently under-represented in professional, world-class orchestras.

calls.description: This is a thematic funding call for research projects about artistic and cultural practices among immigrants to Norway from 1970 to 2000. calls.project_requirements: The project is being implemented in cooperation between Ukrainian and international institution(s) or organisation(s) (museum, gallery, fair, festival, etc. in the country of the project implementation) that have the institutional capacity and experience in implementing similar projects and / or objects of intellectual property that can be used in the process of carrying out the exhibition project and organising the exhibition. The project is being implemented in one of the Ukrainian Institute’s target countries as of 2026 (The Republic of Poland, the Federal Republic of Germany, the French Republic, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the Slovak Republic, the United States of America, the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the Republic of Lithuania, the Republic of South Africa, the Federative Republic of Brazil, the United Mexican States, the Argentine Republic, the Republic of India, the Republic of Indonesia,Hungary). The project showcases Ukrainian photography and/or addresses the overarching themes of the Ukrainian Institute’s activities: Russia’s War Against Ukraine Ukraine’s Recovery and Future Civil Society as the Foundation of Statehood Crimea and the Crimean Tatars Decolonization of culture and reappropriation of cultural heritage Iconic figures, phenomena, and events The start of the project is scheduled no earlier than March 1, 2027.

calls.title: Application for General Projects
calls.description: This funding call supports general visual arts projects such as exhibitions, new productions, publications, and acquisitions for a museum collection. It is part of the Visual Arts programme of Kunststiftung NRW and is aimed at professional artists and institutions/initiatives from North Rhine-Westphalia. Applications are submitted through the application portal, with deadlines twice a year.
calls.project_requirements:
We support, for example, exhibitions, new productions, publications and acquisitions into the collection holdings of a museum.
We do not support database development, database maintenance, acquisition of technical infrastructure, the creation of digitized copies, documentation, prizes, projects from archaeology, or cultural education.

calls.title: Call for Film Projects: SIC 2027
calls.description: SoundImageCulture is a one-year program in Brussels that supports filmmakers, artists and thinkers in the development of a film project. Selected participants work with coaches, peers, international guests, masterclasses and seminars, and present their work publicly at the end of the cycle.
calls.project_requirements:
To be present at the collective sessions
To bring new materials (rushes, edits, try-outs) to every session
To hold at least one meeting (max. 2 hours) with your personal coach in between sessions
To give feedback and assistance to your peers

calls.title: Art Media
calls.description: The Art Media grant supports written and/or spoken word publications that stimulate engagement with and discourse on contemporary visual art. It is aimed at projects such as article series, long reads and podcasts published on public media or online platforms. The grant can support individual practitioners or organisations working in this field, with the amount determined per application based on the budget.
calls.project_requirements: For written and/or spoken word publications. Applications can be submitted for e.g. a series of articles, long reads and podcasts that are published in/on (online) magazines, newspapers, social media channels or other online platforms. The planned publication must be accessible on at least one public medium or platform with appropriate reach. The project may not be directly linked to the applicant’s existing activities (e.g. an article or publication accompanying an exhibition). It is not possible to apply for a grant for television or film productions. It is not possible to apply for a grant for making profiles or portraits of artists.

calls.title: Open Call: Abstract – Exhibition, Magazine Feature, Artist Interview
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit work for a virtual exhibition themed around abstraction. Selected artists may also be featured in the magazine and interviewed, with additional promotion through the organisation’s channels. Prizes include a solo show for first prize and a spot in a future group exhibition for second prize.
calls.project_requirements: The Goddessarts Magazine is excited to announce our upcoming theme: Abstract – a celebration of form, color, movement, and emotion. This exhibition invites artists to explore abstraction in all its powerful forms: gestural brushstrokes, geometric clarity, texture-driven work, conceptual abstraction, emotional expression, and beyond. Whether rooted in chaos or calm, minimalism or maximalism, we want to see how abstraction flows through your creative practice. All mediums and styles except video are welcome & everyone is encouraged to apply.

calls.title: 2027 Curatorial Research Fellowship
calls.description: This fellowship supports exhibition curators developing an original project related to image or photography. It provides a two-phase process: an initial research phase and, subject to approval, a production phase for the exhibition. The grant includes financial support for research and, if approved, additional support for producing the project.
calls.project_requirements:
The selected project will be carried out in two phases:
• research phase focusing on an exhibition project.
• project production – subject to approval.
The curator will be given six months to carry out research, at the end of which they must submit a proposal to the artistic direction team of the Rencontres d’Arles.
Following an artistic evaluation, the Rencontres d’Arles will determine whether or not the project is feasible and approve its presentation format (Phase 2).
• The curator commits to: - select the works that will form the body of the exhibition and determine the rights for their display and reproduction; - design and draft an introductory text for the selection of photographs; - be present during the festival’s opening week and take part in the guided tour of the exhibition.

calls.title: OPEN PROGRAM 2027
calls.description: Open Program 2027 is an open call for artists and collectives to present photography-based projects at the International Festival of Photography in Łódź, Poland, in June 2027. Six selected projects will be exhibited during the festival, giving artists access to an international audience and professional networking opportunities. The program also connects selected artists with the FUTURES photography platform.
calls.project_requirements: Projects created in any photographic or visual medium are welcome.

calls.title: Call for collaborators for the collaborative prototyping laboratory LAB 4 Weird Futures
calls.description: LAB 4 Weird Futures is a multidisciplinary research and collaborative production programme at Medialab Matadero Madrid. It includes a two-week prototyping laboratory, artistic projects, workshops, seminars and public events, and this call is for collaborators to take part in the development of selected projects. The programme culminates in the OpenLAB festival in November 2025.

calls.title: Tel Aviv
calls.description: This residency stipend enables artists from North Rhine-Westphalia to spend six months in a live/work studio in Tel Aviv. It is designed to help them get to know the local art scene, build contacts, and develop new approaches in their artistic practice. The residency also aims to support free experimentation and fair working conditions for visual arts residencies abroad.
calls.project_requirements: a six-month stay in a live/work studio in Tel Aviv

calls.title: Saal Digital European Photo Awards 2026
calls.organisation: Saal Digital in collaboration with Hahnemühle
calls.description: A photography competition inviting photographers across Europe to submit their best work in selected categories. Each category winner receives vouchers from Saal Digital and Hahnemühle, and selected winning images may also be produced as FineArt prints and shown in exhibitions, trade shows, and campaign communication.
calls.project_requirements: You can submit up to 5 photos in total – either all within one category or spread across multiple categories – and increase your chances of winning, as each category has its own Saal Digital voucher prize.

calls.title: FUTURES Talent Call 2027
calls.description: This open call invites photographers and artists working in photography and expanded lens-based practice to join the FUTURES Photography Platform. Selected artists receive a participation fee, international professional conversations, and support to take part in the FUTURES Annual Event in Vienna. The programme also offers visibility, networking, and access to further FUTURES opportunities.

calls.title: Call for individual mobility
calls.organisation: Culture Moves Europe / European Commission / Goethe-Institut
calls.description: This call supports individual mobility projects for artists and cultural professionals in another Creative Europe country. It offers a daily allowance, travel support, and possible top-ups for green mobility, family, visa, and accessibility needs. Applicants choose an international partner and carry out a project that follows two of the objectives: learn, create, explore, or connect.
calls.project_requirements: One project One artistic or cultural project to be carried out in another Creative Europe country, with the support of an international partner. This project must follow 2 of the following objectives: to learn, to create, to explore, or to connect. One international partner The international partner collaborates with the artists and cultural professionals during the project implementation. Applicants chose their own international partner, which can be an individual or an organisation.

calls.title: OPEN CALL FOR PROJECTS LAB 4 WEIRD FUTURES
calls.description: Medialab Matadero is seeking proposals for the Collaborative Prototyping Lab, a creative residency within the year-long LAB 4 Weird Futures programme. Selected projects will be developed collaboratively during an intensive two-week lab in Madrid with mentors and collaborators, and presented at the OpenLAB festival.
calls.project_requirements: The primary activity of each LAB consists of a Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory: an intensive two-week Laboratory to collaboratively develop 5 experimental projects related to the themes that the LAB 4 addresses. Proposals submitted to this call must necessarily be open to the participation of collaborators interested in participating in their development. The Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory will take place from Monday to Friday between November 12th and 26th, 2025, both included, at Medialab's facilities in Matadero Madrid. The public presentation of the developed projects will be between November 27th and 29th, 2025, at the OpenLAB public event. Participation in the lab sessions must be in person and for the entire duration of the programme.

calls.title: AIR - Residencies Abroad 2027 for Visual Artists, Media Artists and Filmmakers
calls.description: This call offers international working residencies in 2027 for visual artists, media artists, and filmmakers. Selected artists can spend time at partner institutions in several countries, with accommodation and/or studio access provided at each destination and a stipend from the City of Salzburg. The programme is intended to support artistic work, exchange, and the development of future projects and collaborations.
calls.project_requirements: At the end of the stay, a written work report including image material must be submitted to the City of Salzburg without being requested. The report should comprehensively present the artistic activities on site and convey to what extent this working stay was relevant for future artistic projects and collaborations and describe them. Works, exhibitions, etc. should be presented in the report using image material.

calls.title: Work and Research Grants
calls.description: This call offers work and research fellowships for individual artistic approaches in visual art for up to 12 months in Germany or abroad. It provides monthly support for research and work projects, with a separate track for international stays that also covers travel costs.
calls.project_requirements:
We award work and research grants for individual artistic approaches of up to 12 months for Germany and abroad.
For further projects (productions, publications, other formats, etc.), a prior consultation and the submission of a written interim report are mandatory.

calls.title: All These Moments – The Future of Artistic Storytelling
calls.organisation: ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar
calls.description: This is the 32nd International Studio Program of the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar. It invites visual artists to propose projects that explore artistic storytelling, memory, authenticity, realism, truthfulness, and related questions, with Weimar as a place of remembrance. Selected artists receive a studio/apartment, a stipend, and the possibility of a later group exhibition.
calls.project_requirements: The International Studio Program is looking for compelling project proposals from visual artists from around the world that address these questions. We welcome experimental forms that embrace Weimar as a place of remembrance—in a good sense as in art and high culture as well as in the bad sense of experiences like the Nazi era. Under consideration are also the small stories of “everyday” life. In order to receive the stipend the artists must live in Weimar during the work period. It is intended that the artists are present during the preparation and for the opening of the exhibition.

calls.title: Photo Contest – Open Call
calls.description: This is a photography competition for the 4th edition of the Annecy Lac Photo festival. Applicants are invited to submit a coherent series of 8 photographs on the theme “Eloge de la lenteur” for possible exhibition at the festival in Annecy.
calls.project_requirements:
For this 4th edition, ALP’ invites you to respond to the call for applications until November 1, 2026 at midnight with a series of photographs, on the theme:
“Praise of slowness”.
Each candidate may send only one application file and only one coherent series of 8 photographs on the theme.
The photographs included in the series will be in JPEG format, without borders, signature, or watermark, with dimensions of 1920 pixels on the longest side.
By participating in this call for applications, the winning photographers commit to being present at the Festival during the opening ceremony on Friday, March 19, 2027 in the evening until Sunday, March 21, 2027.
Photographs captured using cameras, whether film or digital, or smartphones, will be eligible.

calls.title: OPEN CALL Rotterdam 2027
calls.description: Hungry Eye Fair is inviting independent photographers to apply for its Rotterdam 2027 edition. Selected photographers will be presented alongside other photographers at the fair, which takes place in Rotterdam from 17–21 March 2027. The open call is free to apply to, but participation at Hungry Eye Fair requires a contribution.

calls.title: 5th Medialab Matadero Open Call for the Award of Three (3) Residencies within the Annual Situated Research Programme (2027)
calls.description: This open call offers three seven-month research and creation residencies at Medialab Matadero in Madrid. The residencies support experimental, critical, and collaborative projects at the intersection of contemporary art, design, science, technology, and society. Selected projects will also develop a public programme and take part in a final public showcase.
calls.project_requirements:
The residencies will last for seven (7) months and will take place between January and July 2027.
Submitted projects should engage with Medialab Matadero’s lines of work and operate at the margins or intersections of different disciplines, methodologies, and fields of knowledge.
Projects should adhere to the following guidelines:
• Explore potential intersections between art, design, science, technology, and society.
• Contribute to critical reflection on contemporary socio-technical, cultural, ecological, political, or urban challenges.
• Propose collaborative, experimental, situated, or unconventional research methodologies.
• Establish bonds with communities, agents, collectives, citizen initiatives, professional fields, or bodies of knowledge related to the project.
• Incorporate a public dimension through activities involving learning, dissemination, the exchange of knowledge, mediation, or the presentation of the research process.
As part of the residency, each project must develop a public programme related to its research process.
These may take the form of workshops, encounters, working groups, critical sessions, conversations, open laboratories, presentations, or other platforms for collective experimentation.
Comprising between one and six activities, this public programme will be defined and fine-tuned during the residency in dialogue with the Medialab Matadero team, in accordance with the evolution of the research, the needs of the project, and the availability of spaces and resources.
Furthermore, the selected projects must participate in a final public showcase at Medialab Matadero, scheduled to take place between June and July 2027, where they will share the processes, lessons learnt, methodologies, or findings developed during the residency.

calls.title: Hessische Kulturstiftung 2027/2028 travel and residency grants
calls.description: This call offers travel grants, residency grants, and combined residency and travel grants for visual artists. It supports artistic work over several months in destinations such as New York City, London, Paris, Istanbul, and Kyoto, with additional funding available for production or presentation of works. Applications are submitted through the application portal on the page.
calls.project_requirements: For the years 2027 and 2028, the Hessische Kulturstiftung will award altogether 5 travel grants of 3 to 12 months duration for destinations of the recipient’s choice, 7 residency grants of up to 12 months duration (New York City, London, Cité internationale des arts in Paris: 12 months, Istanbul: 6 months), and 2 combined residency and travel grants (residency at the Goethe-Institut Villa Kamogawa in Kyoto: 3 months, followed by an individual travel and work phase: 3 months).

statement:
I am a ceramic artist. I make sculptural ceramics and installations in clay, porcelain and stoneware, fired in wood and gas kilns. My work is about craft knowledge, the hand and the slow time of making, and draws on traditional pottery techniques.

I am looking for residencies with a ceramics studio and kilns, craft and applied arts grants, and exhibition opportunities for contemporary craft and sculpture.

calls.title: Open Call: Monumental Crafts, Ifö Center Group exhibition and Artist Residency
calls.description: Monumental Crafts is a Nordic collaboration that combines a group exhibition with an artist residency focused on large-scale contemporary craft. It offers selected craft artists the chance to develop monumental work, exhibit it at Ifö Center Art Hall, and take part in residency production at Ifö Center in Sweden.
calls.project_requirements:
The project features a group exhibition featuring 15 artists from Sweden, Norway, and Denmark, alongside a residency for three craft makers seeking to work in larger formats and spaces.
Three craft artists – one each from Sweden, Norway, and Denmark – are offered an artist residency at Ifö Center for up to eight weeks during the spring and summer of 2027.
Following the residency period, the newly created monumental works will be showcased in three solo exhibitions at Ifö Center Art Hall.
The Monumental Crafts' group exhibition takes place from 8 May to 21 August 2027, featuring monumental works by fifteen professional craft artists from Sweden, Norway, and Denmark at Ifö Center Art Hall.
Submissions: Up to 3 works per application.

calls.title: Residency open call for artists based in Argentina
calls.description: An eleven-week, fully funded residency for an early-career contemporary visual artist based in Argentina. The residency takes place at Gasworks in London and supports research, artistic experimentation, and the development of new work. It includes studio space, accommodation, travel, a stipend, and curatorial support.
calls.project_requirements:
• All our residencies are self-led, non-prescriptive and process-based; they are about enabling artists to research and develop new work, engage with the city, and build their networks.
• We expect residents to be self-motivated, and to lead on the research and production of their own work, during their time with us.
• An Open Studio event and presentation introducing the work and research developed during the residency, which will take place on Saturday 12 June.

calls.title: GeoMôn - Olion //\ Traces - Commission & Residency
calls.organisation: GeoMôn UNESCO Global Geopark / Plas Bodfa Projects CIC
calls.description: An open call for an artist residency and commission exploring the geology, landscapes and deep time of Ynys Môn. The selected artist will research with GeoMôn UNESCO Global Geopark and develop a new work for the 2027 Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail. The opportunity includes a research period, curatorial support, and public sharing of the process and final work.
calls.project_requirements:
The residency will lead to a new commissioned work for the Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail, 20–21 March 2027 .

Because the Trail takes place across woodland, waterways, historic sites and community spaces, proposals should be sensitive to their environment and appropriate to the site in which they are eventually presented.

The selected artist will take part in an informal online work-in-progress sharing during the residency. Following the Sculpture Trail, they will also participate in a public screening of the project documentation films and panel discussion in May 2027 , bringing together the artists and partner organisations to reflect on the research, process and work that emerged.

If selected, I understand that I will be expected to take part in the residency and research process with GeoMôn and develop a new commissioned work for the 2027 Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail.

calls.title: Different art forms
calls.description: This funding page explains how to apply when an artistic project combines different art forms or does not fit neatly into one category. It supports artistic work that breaks with traditional genres or is hard to define, and it may be assessed by more than one committee if relevant. Applicants are guided on whether to submit one application or split a project into separate subprojects across different funding programmes.
calls.project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.
When you break down your project into several applications, it is important that you also split up your budget, since you are not able to get the same expenses covered by more than one funding programme.
Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.
In some cases, two or more committees join together to fund a grant.
This will often happen, if a project’s budget is too large for one committee to fund it all.

calls.title: Summer Workshops at Haystack Mountain School of Crafts
calls.organisation: The American Scandinavian Foundation and Norwegian Crafts
calls.description: This opportunity offers craft artists spots in the summer workshops at Haystack Mountain School of Crafts in Maine, USA. It supports participation in one- or two-week intensive courses in fields such as ceramics, textiles, metal, wood, and more. The programme is intended to help artists develop their practice and build networks in the USA and internationally.
calls.project_requirements: Duration: Up to 14 consecutive days between June–September 2027, depending on the timings of your selected workshops

calls.title: Contemporary Talents Competition: Water – Wattwiller
calls.description: This is an international contemporary art competition focused on the theme of water. The Foundation acquires selected works, awards prizes to the laureates, and presents the winning artists in an exhibition at its art centre in Wattwiller. Artists may apply with an existing work, and in some cases sculpture or installation projects to be produced.
calls.project_requirements:
The work submitted must be on the theme of Water.
For installations and sculptures, artists may submit either an existing work or a project. If submitting a project, a production budget of no more than €50,000 must be included.
For other artistic forms, only an existing work may be submitted. No additional production budget can be allocated for paintings, drawings, photographs or videos.
The submitted artwork (whether it consists of a single piece or a body of work) must focus exclusively on the theme of water.
Each candidate may submit only one artwork or project per year.
The work submitted must be on the theme of Water.
Each applicant may submit only one work or one project per year.
A work entered into the competition may not be resubmitted in a subsequent year, or at any later date.
Oil paintings on canvas and drawings must not exceed 320 x 210 cm for a single piece. Diptychs and triptychs are accepted

calls.title: Kunsthaus am Wald International Artist in Residence Program Weitenhagen/ Germany
calls.description: This is an artist-in-residence program for the 2027 season at Kunsthaus am Wald in Weitenhagen, Germany. It invites artists from different disciplines and asks applicants to propose a project for the residency period and present their previous work. The location is remote, and site-specific projects are welcome but not required.
calls.project_requirements: Site-specific projects that engage with the spatial context are welcome, though they are not a mandatory requirement for a residency stay.

calls.title: Art Residency Program
calls.description: Can Serrat offers an international art residency program for writers and contemporary artists from around the world. The program provides short- and medium-term residencies with time, space, follow-up, individual and collective support, and a professional network. Some calls include full grants and partial grants.
calls.project_requirements: There is no expectation of a finished product at the end of the residency, and the program does not aim to organize gallery exhibitions.

calls.title: Art Prize 2027
calls.description: The Art Prize 2027 is an open call for contemporary visual artists to propose a new site-specific artwork for permanent outdoor display in Agios Nikolaos, Crete. The selected artist receives a prize and production support to realize a large-scale sculptural installation that will become part of the Foundation’s art collection. The work is unveiled publicly and remains on permanent display.

The Art Prize 2027 invites artists from around the world to submit proposals for a large-scale sculptural installation designed for permanent display in an outdoor setting, serving as a distinctive landmark within the space.

• 2 Before selecting a site for your proposal, please read carefully the relevant information in the file “Characteristics of the Proposed Sites”.

calls.title: Residency open call for Lebanese artists based in Lebanon
calls.description: This is an eleven-week residency at Gasworks in London for a Lebanese artist based in Lebanon. It supports professional development, cultural exchange, and artistic experimentation, and includes studio access, accommodation, travel, a stipend, and curatorial support. The residency is self-led and process-based, with an Open Studio event and presentation at the end.
calls.project_requirements:
• The eleven-week, fully funded residency will take place at Gasworks in London from 7 April – 22 June 2027.
• All our residencies are self-led, non-prescriptive and process-based; they are about enabling artists to research and develop new work, engage with the city, and build their networks.
• We provide administrative, pastoral, and curatorial support throughout the residency, but we expect residents to be self-motivated, and to lead on the research and production of their own work, during their time with us.
• An Open Studio event and presentation introducing the work and research developed during the residency, which will take place on Saturday 12 June.

calls.title: 33rd International Studio Program of the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar OPEN CALL 2026: On Absence
calls.organisation: ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit project proposals for the 33rd International Studio Program in Weimar. The 2026 theme is “On Absence,” and selected artists will take part in an international studio program connected to the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar.
calls.project_requirements: submit proposals for projects that explore absence and the absent through art, rethink absence in radically new ways, challenge it aesthetically, or use it as a tool for social critique.

calls.title: Creative Steps for Individuals
calls.description: Creative Steps for Individuals is a funding opportunity for artists and creative professionals in Wales who have experienced barriers to careers within the arts. It supports professional, business and organisational development rather than the creation of new work. Applicants can use the grant for activities such as mentoring, training, networking, business development, website development, or setting up a new organisation.
calls.project_requirements: Creative Steps for Individuals is for supporting career development, and NOT for creating new work or project delivery. Please bear in mind that you need to allow a minimum of 12 working weeks between the deadline date and the start date of your project. We cannot fund proposals that are already happening so we won’t accept your application if your proposal’s start date will come before we’ve had the opportunity to assess your application.

calls.title: OPEN CALL FOR PROJECTS LAB 4 WEIRD FUTURES
calls.description: Medialab Matadero is seeking proposals for the Collaborative Prototyping Lab, a creative residency within the year-long LAB 4 Weird Futures programme. Selected projects will be developed collaboratively during an intensive two-week lab in Madrid with mentors and collaborators, and presented at the OpenLAB festival.
calls.project_requirements: The primary activity of each LAB consists of a Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory: an intensive two-week Laboratory to collaboratively develop 5 experimental projects related to the themes that the LAB 4 addresses. Proposals submitted to this call must necessarily be open to the participation of collaborators interested in participating in their development. The Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory will take place from Monday to Friday between November 12th and 26th, 2025, both included, at Medialab's facilities in Matadero Madrid. The public presentation of the developed projects will be between November 27th and 29th, 2025, at the OpenLAB public event. Participation in the lab sessions must be in person and for the entire duration of the programme.

calls.title: Consultants and Specialists Grant
calls.description: DGARTES is inviting interested specialists to register for its pool of consultants and experts. The people selected from this pool may take part in assessment and monitoring committees for arts funding programmes. The page explains the profile DGARTES is looking for and provides a registration request form.
calls.project_requirements: The consultants and specialists who make up the appraisal committees and monitoring committees of DGARTES are responsible, respectively, for appraising the projects and artistic activities applying for financial support, as well as evaluating their implementation.

calls.title: Essere Residency
calls.description: Essere Residency is an international artist residency program for creative and scholarly practitioners across literature, visual arts, performance art, arts and humanities, philosophy and research, and food art. It offers two-week residencies and includes partial fellowships for selected applicants.
calls.project_requirements:
A description in English of the project that the applicant would pursue during her/his stay

1-5 relevant samples of recent work.

Residencies are 2 weeks long.

calls.title: Residencies / Biodesign Research Residency / BIZIRIK / EKHŌ / BILME
calls.description: The Basque Biodesign Center offers several research residencies focused on biodesign, biofashion, and textile innovation. Residents get access to specialized labs, machinery, technical and teaching support, and a collaborative environment to develop concepts, prototypes, and sustainable materials. The program connects design, technology, craft, and local resources, with residencies aimed at emerging creators as well as experienced textile practitioners.
calls.project_requirements:
Design and innovation for the development of new uses with local waste will be the axis of the project. The main goal of biodesign research residency is to develop new sustainable products, new materials as a way to transform, revaluate and unite rural and urban lifestyles using local raw materials.

The main goal of this residency is to empower experienced professionals to push the boundaries of digital jacquard design in order to develop new sustainable textile structures and alternatives. We seek to transform the fashion industry by bridging cutting-edge technology with the use of novel materials, upcycling local resources, and connecting artisanal heritage with the design of the future.

calls.title: EFFEA Call #5
calls.description: EFFEA Call #5 invites festivals and artists to apply for a residency programme. It supports collaborations between lead and partner festivals and an emerging artist, with the application requiring a proposed residency setup, motivation, and budget information.

calls.title: Heneb: the Trust for Welsh Archaeology Commission
calls.description: This open call invites artists and makers to develop new work through a research residency with Heneb: the Trust for Welsh Archaeology. The selected artist will explore archaeology, landscape, and traces of human activity around Aberlleiniog, leading to a commissioned work for the 2027 Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail. The process includes research, exchange, and public sharing, with support from the organisers.
calls.project_requirements: The residency will lead to a new commissioned work for the Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail, 20–21 March 2027 . We welcome sculpture, installation, sound, performance, participatory work, moving image and interdisciplinary approaches. The work might take the form of an object, an encounter, an intervention, an activity or something we haven't anticipated. Because the Trail takes place across woodland, waterways, historic sites and community spaces, proposals should be sensitive to their environment and appropriate to the site in which they are eventually presented. The final form and location of the work will be developed during the residency. The selected artist will take part in an informal online work-in-progress sharing during the residency. Following the Sculpture Trail, they will also participate in a public screening of the project documentation films and panel discussion in May 2027 , bringing together the artists and partner organisations to reflect on the research, process and work that emerged.

calls.title: Schleich-Lentz Foundation Grant
calls.description: This is a call for projects supporting the creation of a ceramic project. It offers a grant to help realize the project, with funding paid in several instalments to the selected artist or collective. The call includes a jury review and requires a final report on the use of the grant.
calls.project_requirements: The grant aims to support the realization of a ceramics project. / Precise statement of intent describing the artistic project, the research that the artist or collective wishes to undertake, as well as the media envisaged (issues, objectives, techniques, areas of work…) / Provisional budget (no dissemination expense is taken into account within the framework of the grant) / Provisional financing plan which must mention the other grants applied for or obtained and the level of financial participation of any disseminators (galleries, art centers, museum) in the production. / The selected artist or group of artists undertakes to present to the National Cultural Fund a detailed report on the use of the grant, as well as a financial statement. This report must be submitted within a maximum period of three months after the project end date indicated in the application.

calls.title: International Studio Programme
calls.description: The International Studio Programme at Künstlerhaus Bethanien offers artists from around the world the chance to develop and deepen their artistic practice in Berlin. It provides individualized support, studio-based work, and opportunities to present work through open studios, studio visits, and exhibitions. The page also announces a Curatorial Fellow Program 2026 that brings selected curators, researchers, and artists into a year-long curatorial accompaniment within the residency program.

calls.title: Apply for residency
calls.description: This is a residency opportunity at the Danish Art Workshops for professional artists, designers, craftspeople and art restorers who need access to large-format workshops and facilities. It offers studio and workshop access, accommodation in a guest flat, and consultation, with projects in either development/research or production/completion. Residencies can support work for exhibition, decoration, or other cultural activity in Denmark.
calls.project_requirements:
• DEVELOPMENT Projects deriving from material based, artistic development / research including material research, prototype production or other kinds of “work in process”.
• Projects that resemble research, exploration, and innovation.
• The purpose of the project must be well described.
• PRODUCTION Projects, that focus on production and completion of works for exhibition, decoration etc.
• It may be single works or a full exhibition.
• Projects targeted a public review in- or outside of Denmark.
• You can apply for a residency of up to six months.
• The length of the residency has to fit your project.
• Please state if you are flexible on the exact period of time or the studio you have applied for.
• In some cases, the committee assesses that a project can be done in a shorter period of time and this might result in a shorter term of residency, than was applied for.

calls.title: All These Moments – The Future of Artistic Storytelling
calls.organisation: ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar
calls.description: This is the 32nd International Studio Program of the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar. It invites visual artists to propose projects that explore artistic storytelling, memory, authenticity, realism, truthfulness, and related questions, with Weimar as a place of remembrance. Selected artists receive a studio/apartment, a stipend, and the possibility of a later group exhibition.
calls.project_requirements: The International Studio Program is looking for compelling project proposals from visual artists from around the world that address these questions. We welcome experimental forms that embrace Weimar as a place of remembrance—in a good sense as in art and high culture as well as in the bad sense of experiences like the Nazi era. Under consideration are also the small stories of “everyday” life. In order to receive the stipend the artists must live in Weimar during the work period. It is intended that the artists are present during the preparation and for the opening of the exhibition.

calls.title: Atlasarts
calls.description: Atlasarts is a research and creative residency programme for Moroccan artists. It offers three-month residencies in Paris with studio accommodation, a living allowance, and opportunities for meetings and professional networking.
calls.project_requirements: The residencies last for three months, starting in January 2027. Please note that laureates undertake to comply with the conditions set out in the Cité internationale des arts’ internal regulations.

calls.title: Residency in Berlin, Bethanien
calls.organisation: The Swedish Arts Grants Committee’s International Programme for Visual and Applied Artists, IASPIS
calls.description: This residency programme offers artists a studio, housing, and a stipend for a stay at Künstlerhaus Bethanien in Berlin. It is intended to support artists’ opportunities to create, develop, and build contacts outside Sweden. The residency runs in collaboration with Künstlerhaus Bethanien, a studio programme and project workshop for international contemporary art.

calls.title: Pilchuck Sessions 2
calls.description: Norwegian Crafts and the American-Scandinavian Foundation offer craft artists places in the summer programmes at Pilchuck Glass School in Washington, USA. The opportunity provides intensive training in glass techniques, networking, and time to develop artistic practice in an international setting. Two artists are selected for up to 18 consecutive days between June and September 2026.
calls.project_requirements: Duration: Up to 18 consecutive days between June – September 2026, depending on the timings of your selected programme.

calls.title: Art Explora x Cité internationale des arts
calls.organisation: The Art Explora Foundation and the Cité internationale des arts
calls.description: A residency programme for French and international artists and researchers that supports projects engaging with contemporary issues such as new technologies, art and science, and environmental and social questions. It offers two formats: a SOLO programme for artists and a Collective programme for collectives, researchers, and curators. Residents receive studio space, a living allowance, a production grant, and travel to Paris.
calls.project_requirements: The programme invites candidates to propose a project that questions contemporary issues, including new technologies, the links between art and science, and environmental and social issues. Please explain why being based in France is necessary to the development of your project (conceptual, geographical and practical aspects, social ties, etc.).

calls.title: Open Call: Abstract – Exhibition, Magazine Feature, Artist Interview
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit work for a virtual exhibition themed around abstraction. Selected artists may also be featured in the magazine and interviewed, with additional promotion through the organisation’s channels. Prizes include a solo show for first prize and a spot in a future group exhibition for second prize.
calls.project_requirements: The Goddessarts Magazine is excited to announce our upcoming theme: Abstract – a celebration of form, color, movement, and emotion. This exhibition invites artists to explore abstraction in all its powerful forms: gestural brushstrokes, geometric clarity, texture-driven work, conceptual abstraction, emotional expression, and beyond. Whether rooted in chaos or calm, minimalism or maximalism, we want to see how abstraction flows through your creative practice. All mediums and styles except video are welcome & everyone is encouraged to apply.

calls.title: CALL FOR APPLICATIONS FOR BRITISH CREATORS-EDUCATORS - LEVADURA PROGRAMME OF RESIDENCES
calls.organisation: Madrid Destino Cultura Turismo y Negocio S.A.
calls.description: This is an open call for a British creator-educator to take part in Levadura, a residency programme in Madrid. The selected participant will develop a contemporary creative arts project with CentroCentro Cibeles and one or more primary schools in the Madrid municipal area. The programme focuses on introducing contemporary art concepts and methods into education through participatory workshops with pupils and teachers.
calls.project_requirements:
The applicant will undertake a residency at CentroCentro Cibeles from 4th until the 31 st of May 2015, during which they will be required to run a series of workshops with primary school pupils from schools in the municipality of Madrid.

The description must include the following information:
• The age range at which the project is aimed, bearing in mind that in Spain primary education covers from 6 to 12 years of age.
• Project plan and timescales, with information such as number of sessions and how long they last (taking into account that the school day runs from 9am to 4pm).
• Approximate budget and description of the material to be used, which will have to be approved by MADRID DESTINO

calls.title: Apply for artist-in-residence
calls.description: Konstepidemin offers international guest studios for artists to live and work in Gothenburg. The residency includes a studio space, bedroom, kitchen and bathroom, and artists also get access to shared facilities such as a printer/scanner/copy machine and a graphics workshop. Applications are accepted throughout the year for stays of one to six months.
calls.project_requirements: Konstepidemin’s five guest studios can be rented for periods of one to six months, and a minimum of one month is required. Please plan ahead and make sure to apply with some flexibility regarding your desired dates for residency. Longer periods are prioritized.

calls.title: Research Residency Programme
calls.description: The Research Residency Programme offers participants time and space for site-based research, dialogue, and the development of new ideas. It brings together interdisciplinary practitioners for an intensive week of workshops, discussions, reflection, and collaborative research focused on the intersections of Art, Science & Technology. The programme welcomes a small cohort each year and covers participation, accommodation, and travel costs.

calls.title: Artist Basic
calls.description: Artist Basic is a grant for visual artists to support the development of their professional practice and the creation of new work. It offers funding that can be used for research, experimentation, materials or equipment, commissions, and participation in exhibitions or events. The grant is intended to help artists expand their oeuvre, visibility, and cultural entrepreneurship.
calls.project_requirements:
For creating work.
That can include research, experimentation, or the purchase of new materials or equipment. Or it can help with the execution of a commission and/or participation in exhibitions or events in the Netherlands or abroad.

calls.title: MA Performance Practices (Autumn 2027)
calls.description: Applications are open for entry into the MA Performance Practices master’s degree programme starting in Autumn 2027. The programme focuses on practice-as-research and brings together performance art, choreography, contemporary theatre, experimental dance, and visual art. It emphasizes critical inquiry, politics and ethics, and collaborative learning with peers, guests, and researchers.

calls.title: Application form – studio at Konstepidemin
calls.description: Konstepidemin is accepting applications for a studio space at its art center in Gothenburg. The form asks applicants to indicate their preferred studio size and area of interest, and it also notes community duties connected to being an artist at Konstepidemin. Applicants must submit a CV and a personal letter describing their practice and why they want a studio there.
calls.project_requirements: As an artist at Konstepidemin you are required to take part in the board, the culture committee, or one of our work sections: gallery, studio, stage, kids and youths, the international group, outdoor/gardening. Check area of interest (more than one is allowed).

calls.title: Open Call for Tokyo Wonder Site residency programs
calls.description: Tokyo Wonder Site Residency offers artist-in-residence programs for international creators in creative fields such as art, design, music and architecture. The page announces two residency programs for 2018: an International Creator Residency Program and a Research Residency Program. The residencies provide time and space for creation and research, along with opportunities to present work and exchange ideas.
calls.project_requirements:
• Residency Period: 3 months
• Residency Period: About 6 weeks

calls.title: 5th Medialab Matadero Open Call for the Award of Three (3) Residencies within the Annual Situated Research Programme (2027)
calls.description: This open call offers three seven-month research and creation residencies at Medialab Matadero in Madrid. The residencies support experimental, critical, and collaborative projects at the intersection of contemporary art, design, science, technology, and society. Selected projects will also develop a public programme and take part in a final public showcase.
calls.project_requirements:
The residencies will last for seven (7) months and will take place between January and July 2027.
Submitted projects should engage with Medialab Matadero’s lines of work and operate at the margins or intersections of different disciplines, methodologies, and fields of knowledge.
Projects should adhere to the following guidelines:
• Explore potential intersections between art, design, science, technology, and society.
• Contribute to critical reflection on contemporary socio-technical, cultural, ecological, political, or urban challenges.
• Propose collaborative, experimental, situated, or unconventional research methodologies.
• Establish bonds with communities, agents, collectives, citizen initiatives, professional fields, or bodies of knowledge related to the project.
• Incorporate a public dimension through activities involving learning, dissemination, the exchange of knowledge, mediation, or the presentation of the research process.
As part of the residency, each project must develop a public programme related to its research process.
These may take the form of workshops, encounters, working groups, critical sessions, conversations, open laboratories, presentations, or other platforms for collective experimentation.
Comprising between one and six activities, this public programme will be defined and fine-tuned during the residency in dialogue with the Medialab Matadero team, in accordance with the evolution of the research, the needs of the project, and the availability of spaces and resources.
Furthermore, the selected projects must participate in a final public showcase at Medialab Matadero, scheduled to take place between June and July 2027, where they will share the processes, lessons learnt, methodologies, or findings developed during the residency.

statement:
I am a theatre director and playwright. I make text-based and devised theatre with an independent company, often on political and social topics such as housing and work. Our productions tour small venues and festivals.

I am looking for funding for theatre productions, residencies for theatre makers to develop new plays, playwriting competitions and festivals that programme independent theatre.

calls.title: ENTER
calls.description: ENTER is the Nordic Culture Fund’s programme for ambitious ideas that can open up new perspectives and set new things in motion through collaboration. It supports initiatives that want space to experiment, learn as they go, and test new directions before the outcome is fully clear. The programme offers funding for projects with a Nordic connection and a strong role for arts and culture.
calls.project_requirements: To be eligible for funding through ENTER, your initiative must have a Nordic anchoring and be built on collaboration across borders. Arts and culture must be a significant part of the initiative, but we also encourage collaborations with other sectors, practices and areas of society. ENTER does not support initiatives whose primary purpose is: education or study visits participation in conferences, festivals, events or similar activities tours or travelling exhibitions productions or publications organisational running costs or core funding construction projects or the purchase of technical equipment for day-to-day operations You can only apply for activities that take place after you have received the funding decision from the Nordic Culture Fund. Your initiative must be completed and reported on no later than one year after the stated start date. As a general rule, the project periods for ENTER cannot be extended.

calls.title: Residencies 2027/28
calls.description: The Landis & Gyr Foundation offers artist residencies in Budapest, Bucharest, London, Sofia and Belgrade, as well as Zug residencies for writers and literary translators. The programme provides accommodation and a monthly stipend, and some locations also offer access to studio or rehearsal space. Applicants can choose one location and indicate preferred time periods.
calls.project_requirements: The desired time period (first and second preference) should also be stated.

calls.title: ‘Quartieri di Vita’ theatre festival (Naples) is looking for a creator/director
calls.organisation: Festival Quartieri Di Vita, Flanders Arts Institute, Flemish Diplomatic Representation in Rome
calls.description: This call invites a creator/director from Flanders to develop a two-week co-creation workshop with vulnerable groups in the Campania region, as part of the ‘Quartieri di Vita’ theatre festival in Naples. The selected artist will work with an Italian director and present short performance sessions at the end of the workshop. The programme also aims to build links between socially engaged practices in Flanders and Naples.
calls.project_requirements: The creator/director from Flanders with a socially engaged practice is invited to work with one vulnerable group from 19 to 29 November 2026 . Examples of vulnerable groups include young people at risk, women who are victims of violence, people from migrant backgrounds, people with different abilities, or people with mental health vulnerabilities. The group of participants will be selected based on the chosen candidate and the workshop proposal, in collaboration with an Italian director. The workshop will be conducted in Italian as not all participants speak English. An Italian–English interpreter will be provided. Knowledge of English is therefore essential. The workshop will last between 4 and 6 hours per day. Short performance sessions are planned at the end of the workshop (27–30 November). The workshop will be prepared online in collaboration with the Italian director.

calls.title: Create and Engage
calls.description: Create and Engage funds the development, creation and delivery of high-quality arts experiences that help creative individuals and organisations engage with and connect to the public. It supports projects involving creation, presentation, programming, touring, community participation, and training and professional development for organisations. There are two levels of award, and projects must align with the fund’s priorities and supported artforms.
calls.project_requirements: Applications must be focussed on the artforms that we support. Your project must take place mainly in Wales. We can only fund activities or events taking place outside of Wales where you can demonstrate longer-term benefit to individuals and communities within Wales. We can consider funding some international activity as part of a wider project if a clear rationale is given. Your project must complement and enhance your usual programme of activity. This means it should not be part of your core activity or include core costs. Your proposal should be for new activity, or work linked to an upcoming opportunity (such as a specific commission, collaboration, presentation, development period, or public engagement activity). Your project must involve working with others. Your project must be time limited. This means it has a definite start and end date. You must have other funding to contribute to the overall costs of your project. You must allow adequate lead time.

calls.title: EFFEA Call #5
calls.description: EFFEA Call #5 invites festivals and artists to apply for a residency programme. It supports collaborations between lead and partner festivals and an emerging artist, with the application requiring a proposed residency setup, motivation, and budget information.

calls.title: Independent performing arts – project (theatre)
calls.description: Grants for the artistic production and presentation of theatre, both individual projects and multi-year projects.
