calls.title: Temporarily Out of Place
calls.description: Treehouse NDSM is announcing an open call for its next exhibition, Temporarily Out of Place. The exhibition explores alternatives to current production systems and invites proposals that respond to large-scale challenges and contribute to alternative circular systems. Selected works may include performance, painting, making, installation, and video.
calls.project_requirements: Apply for the open call with a proposal that offers situated responses to large-scale challenges and contributes to the development of alternative circular systems. Submissions may span various media, including performance, painting, making, installation, and video.

calls.title: Seeking Support
calls.description: DGARTES presents open funding opportunities for artistic activity through its support programmes and funding lines. The page points applicants to the candidate support area and the management platform where application forms are available. It also links to the annual declaration listing the open calls and funding amounts for 2026.

calls.title: Visual art – production and dissemination – exhibition venues
calls.description: Grants to produce and disseminate visual art.

calls.title: Art Commission
calls.description: This grant supports commissions for visual artists to create new publicly accessible artworks or longer collaborations that result in new work. It is aimed at projects visible to the public in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. The fund can also support a development phase for commissioners who need help preparing a plan or sketch phase.
calls.project_requirements: With this grant, anyone without intention to sell the work can commission visual artists to create new works of art accessible to the public in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. The work to be commissioned must be accessible to the public and presented in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. The work may not be for profit. A realistic fee for the artist is mandatory, and must be included in the budget, in addition to the production costs. If the project concerns a permanent work of art, it may not be moved or traded without permission of the Mondriaan Fund. In that case, realistic compensation must also be paid to the artist.

calls.title: Art in public space - Annuale
calls.organisation: Department of Culture of the City of Munich
calls.description: This is a competition for freely accessible art projects in public urban spaces in Munich. Selected projects can receive support for temporary art interventions as part of Public Art München’s 2027 Annuale programme.
calls.project_requirements:
The artistic projects will take place temporarily in public spaces in 2027
Organisation (including permits) and implementation are carried out by the artists
The projects must take into account Public Art München’s Sustainability Roadmap ( https://www.publicartmuenchen.de/ueber-uns/ )
This must take place in Munich’s urban space during 2027, with free admission.

calls.title: Open Call for Tokyo Wonder Site residency programs
calls.description: Tokyo Wonder Site Residency offers artist-in-residence programs for international creators in creative fields such as art, design, music and architecture. The page announces two residency programs for 2018: an International Creator Residency Program and a Research Residency Program. The residencies provide time and space for creation and research, along with opportunities to present work and exchange ideas.
calls.project_requirements:
• Residency Period: 3 months
• Residency Period: About 6 weeks

calls.title: Hessische Kulturstiftung 2027/2028 travel and residency grants
calls.description: This call offers travel grants, residency grants, and combined residency and travel grants for visual artists. It supports artistic work over several months in destinations such as New York City, London, Paris, Istanbul, and Kyoto, with additional funding available for production or presentation of works. Applications are submitted through the application portal on the page.
calls.project_requirements: For the years 2027 and 2028, the Hessische Kulturstiftung will award altogether 5 travel grants of 3 to 12 months duration for destinations of the recipient’s choice, 7 residency grants of up to 12 months duration (New York City, London, Cité internationale des arts in Paris: 12 months, Istanbul: 6 months), and 2 combined residency and travel grants (residency at the Goethe-Institut Villa Kamogawa in Kyoto: 3 months, followed by an individual travel and work phase: 3 months).

calls.title: Artist Project
calls.description: The Artist Project grant supports visual artists who want to realise a concrete artistic plan within a defined working period. It can cover project costs for new work, collaboration, travel, research, mentoring, or a residency in the Netherlands or abroad. The grant is intended to help artists develop work that can strengthen the quality and visibility of contemporary visual art.
calls.project_requirements: To implement a specific plan, tied to a clear working period. It can also involve collaboration. The grant is to help cover project costs, such as the execution of a concrete plan for new work, a collaboration, a period of travel or a working period. It may also entail research, mentoring or a stay at a residency in the Netherlands or abroad. The duration of the contribution must be justified by a global timeline, included in your plan. Applicants are obliged to contribute at least 10% of the total sum being requested from the Mondriaan Fund. This can be in the form of a personal investment, contributions from third parties, an interest-free loan from Fonds Kwadraat or a contribution raised through crowdfunding. This means that the contribution from the Mondriaan Fund will be for a maximum of 90% of the costs that are eligible for the grant. If the application involves another party, such as an art venue, museum, gallery, company or client, the financial contribution from this party must be in acceptable proportion to the contribution requested from the Mondriaan Fund. Cultural institutions are expected to subscribe to the Fair Practice Code. Compliance with the Fair Practice Code automatically means that the institution implements the Guideline for Artists’ Fees. What is eligible: The cost of materials specifically related to the project. Rental of equipment and materials. If equipment is purchased that is strictly necessary for the project, the depreciation costs can be included in the budget. Travel expenses for a return flight, train journey or mileage allowance to and from the main location as stated in the application. Local travel expenses are part of the contribution covering time investment. Hiring third parties (including travel and accommodation expenses, if applicable). Residency expenses: Please note that the contribution covering time investment is halved if a residency fee is included in the budget, or if it becomes apparent that the residency covers the following expenses: accommodation and meals. In the case of an artist’s book, the contribution may only be used for a special publication that can be considered an autonomous work of art in its own right and is produced in an edition of no more than 3 copies. The Artist Project grant may not be used for other publications, but the Publication grant is available for such projects. What is not eligible: Regular expenses, such as ongoing housing costs and child care are not eligible for a grant. The grant is not intended for work for an organisation, for regular work activities, exhibition costs or other costs of presenting work. The grant cannot be used to put previously produced work back into production, to frame work or transfer it to a different medium. Costs associated with a stay abroad and that are covered by the contribution for time investment include accommodation, meals and local travel expenses. An application can be made for these costs for third parties involved with the project. The Artist Project grant may not be used for a working period in a guest studio in the Netherlands or abroad if this studio is offered in the Mondriaan Fund’s Residency The Artist Project grant may not be used for activities or a project at institutions/art venues receiving long-term financial support from one of the Rijkscultuurfondsen (public cultural funds) or the Basic Cultural Infrastructure (BIS), unless it concerns non-standard programming.

calls.title: OPEN CALL FOR PROJECTS LAB 4 WEIRD FUTURES
calls.description: Medialab Matadero is seeking proposals for the Collaborative Prototyping Lab, a creative residency within the year-long LAB 4 Weird Futures programme. Selected projects will be developed collaboratively during an intensive two-week lab in Madrid with mentors and collaborators, and presented at the OpenLAB festival.
calls.project_requirements: The primary activity of each LAB consists of a Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory: an intensive two-week Laboratory to collaboratively develop 5 experimental projects related to the themes that the LAB 4 addresses. Proposals submitted to this call must necessarily be open to the participation of collaborators interested in participating in their development. The Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory will take place from Monday to Friday between November 12th and 26th, 2025, both included, at Medialab's facilities in Matadero Madrid. The public presentation of the developed projects will be between November 27th and 29th, 2025, at the OpenLAB public event. Participation in the lab sessions must be in person and for the entire duration of the programme.

calls.project_requirements: The residency will lead to a new commissioned work for the Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail, 20–21 March 2027 . We welcome sculpture, installation, sound, performance, participatory work, moving image and interdisciplinary approaches. The work might take the form of an object, an encounter, an intervention, an activity or something we haven't anticipated. Following the Sculpture Trail, they will also participate in a public screening of the project documentation films and panel discussion in May 2027 , bringing together the artists and partner organisations to reflect on the research, process and work that emerged. If selected, I understand that I will be expected to take part in the residency and research process with North Wales Rivers Trust and develop a new commissioned work for the 2027 Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail.

calls.title: Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail Open Call 2027
calls.description: The Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail Open Call invites artists, makers and creative practitioners to propose work for a two-day sculpture trail in the landscapes around Llangoed and Aberlleiniog. Selected projects can include sculpture, installation, sound, performance, moving image, participatory work, workshops, walks, craft, environmental projects and interdisciplinary approaches. The trail takes place across woodland, waterways, castle, coastline and community spaces, and participants may receive support toward materials or project costs.
calls.project_requirements: We invite artists, makers, craftspeople, environmentalists, performers and creative practitioners to propose work that engages with these landscapes in imaginative ways. This might mean responding directly to a particular site, exploring its histories or ecologies, creating an encounter for visitors, or bringing a work into a new context. Work can be new, existing, adapted or reworked. The work should be able to be presented safely and practically within the Trail. Artists are responsible for installing their own work. Friday 19 March 2027 — Installation Day All work must be completely installed by 15:00 so that we can undertake our final site and risk assessment. Saturday 20 + Sunday 21 March 2027 — Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail Work should remain in place for both days. Monday 22 March 2027 — Deinstallation All work must be removed by 19:00.

calls.title: Heneb: the Trust for Welsh Archaeology Commission
calls.description: This open call invites artists and makers to develop new work through a research residency with Heneb: the Trust for Welsh Archaeology. The selected artist will explore archaeology, landscape, and traces of human activity around Aberlleiniog, leading to a commissioned work for the 2027 Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail. calls.project_requirements: The residency will lead to a new commissioned work for the Aberlleiniog Sculpture Trail, 20–21 March 2027 . We welcome sculpture, installation, sound, performance, participatory work, moving image and interdisciplinary approaches. The work might take the form of an object, an encounter, an intervention, an activity or something we haven't anticipated. Because the Trail takes place across woodland, waterways, historic sites and community spaces, proposals should be sensitive to their environment and appropriate to the site in which they are eventually presented. The final form and location of the work will be developed during the residency. The selected artist will take part in an informal online work-in-progress sharing during the residency. calls.title: Creative Steps for Individuals
calls.description: Creative Steps for Individuals is a funding opportunity for artists and creative professionals in Wales who have experienced barriers to careers within the arts. It supports professional, business and organisational development rather than the creation of new work. Applicants can use the grant for activities such as mentoring, training, networking, business development, website development, or setting up a new organisation.
calls.project_requirements: Creative Steps for Individuals is for supporting career development, and NOT for creating new work or project delivery. Please bear in mind that you need to allow a minimum of 12 working weeks between the deadline date and the start date of your project. We cannot fund proposals that are already happening so we won’t accept your application if your proposal’s start date will come before we’ve had the opportunity to assess your application.

statement:
I am a performance artist. My live works use the body, endurance and ritual, and often involve the audience. I work across performance art, video and installation, and my themes are gender, queerness and care.

I am looking for residencies for performance and live art, open calls for performance festivals, and grants for interdisciplinary and experimental projects.

calls.title: Different art forms
calls.description: This funding page explains how to apply when an artistic project combines different art forms or does not fit neatly into one category. It supports artistic work that breaks with traditional genres or is hard to define, and it may be assessed by more than one committee if relevant. Applicants are guided on whether to submit one application or split a project into separate subprojects across different funding programmes.
calls.project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.
When you break down your project into several applications, it is important that you also split up your budget, since you are not able to get the same expenses covered by more than one funding programme.
Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.
In some cases, two or more committees join together to fund a grant.
This will often happen, if a project’s budget is too large for one committee to fund it all.

calls.title: International Studio Programme
calls.description: The International Studio Programme at Künstlerhaus Bethanien offers artists from around the world the chance to develop and deepen their artistic practice in Berlin. It provides individualized support, studio-based work, and opportunities to present work through open studios, studio visits, and exhibitions. The page also announces a Curatorial Fellow Program 2026 that brings selected curators, researchers, and artists into a year-long curatorial accompaniment within the residency program.

calls.title: Apply for residency
calls.description: This is a residency opportunity at the Danish Art Workshops for professional artists, designers, craftspeople and art restorers who need access to large-format workshops and facilities. It offers studio and workshop access, accommodation in a guest flat, and consultation, with projects in either development/research or production/completion. Residencies can support work for exhibition, decoration, or other cultural activity in Denmark.
calls.project_requirements:
• DEVELOPMENT Projects deriving from material based, artistic development / research including material research, prototype production or other kinds of “work in process”.
• Projects that resemble research, exploration, and innovation.
• The purpose of the project must be well described.
• PRODUCTION Projects, that focus on production and completion of works for exhibition, decoration etc.
• It may be single works or a full exhibition.
• Projects targeted a public review in- or outside of Denmark.
• You can apply for a residency of up to six months.
• The length of the residency has to fit your project.
• Please state if you are flexible on the exact period of time or the studio you have applied for.
• In some cases, the committee assesses that a project can be done in a shorter period of time and this might result in a shorter term of residency, than was applied for.

calls.title: EFFEA Call #5
calls.description: EFFEA Call #5 invites festivals and artists to apply for a residency programme. It supports collaborations between lead and partner festivals and an emerging artist, with the application requiring a proposed residency setup, motivation, and budget information.

calls.title: MA Performance Practices (Autumn 2027)
calls.description: Applications are open for entry into the MA Performance Practices master’s degree programme starting in Autumn 2027. The programme focuses on practice-as-research and brings together performance art, choreography, contemporary theatre, experimental dance, and visual art. It emphasizes critical inquiry, politics and ethics, and collaborative learning with peers, guests, and researchers.

calls.description: Medialab Matadero is seeking proposals for the Collaborative Prototyping Lab, a creative residency within the year-long LAB 4 Weird Futures programme. Participation in the lab sessions must be in person and for the entire duration of the programme.

calls.title: DancEUA Artist-in-Residence
calls.description: An international artist-in-residence programme for emerging dance artists from partner countries within the dancEUA project. It offers residencies in Sweden with studio access, mentorship, and a work-in-progress presentation for local audiences. The programme supports the development of new or ongoing dance and performing arts projects.
calls.project_requirements:
Each residency will host up to three dance projects, with one dance artist from Ukraine and two from other partner countries in each period.
The residencies welcome both solo and duet projects and give artists the chance to work with a professional mentor who will support them in developing their artistic creations.
The program culminates in a work-in-progress presentation, allowing artists to share their artistic works with the local audience of Tanum.

calls.title: Residency in Berlin, Bethanien
calls.organisation: The Swedish Arts Grants Committee’s International Programme for Visual and Applied Artists, IASPIS
calls.description: This residency programme offers artists a studio, housing, and a stipend for a stay at Künstlerhaus Bethanien in Berlin. It is intended to support artists’ opportunities to create, develop, and build contacts outside Sweden. The residency runs in collaboration with Künstlerhaus Bethanien, a studio programme and project workshop for international contemporary art.

calls.title: Kunsthaus am Wald International Artist in Residence Program Weitenhagen/ Germany
calls.description: This is an artist-in-residence program for the 2027 season at Kunsthaus am Wald in Weitenhagen, Germany. It invites artists from different disciplines and asks applicants to propose a project for the residency period and present their previous work. The location is remote, and site-specific projects are welcome but not required.
calls.project_requirements: Site-specific projects that engage with the spatial context are welcome, though they are not a mandatory requirement for a residency stay.

calls.title: Essere Residency
calls.description: Essere Residency is an international artist residency program for creative and scholarly practitioners across literature, visual arts, performance art, arts and humanities, philosophy and research, and food art. It offers two-week residencies and includes partial fellowships for selected applicants.
calls.project_requirements:
A description in English of the project that the applicant would pursue during her/his stay

1-5 relevant samples of recent work.

Residencies are 2 weeks long.

calls.title: Open Call for performers and costume- & fashion designers
calls.description: This open call invites performers to propose a performance, character, or small happening for the Dress-up-tea-Party, centered on the social aspects of drinking tea. It also invites fashion and costume designers to propose a selection of pieces or costumes to be worn during the event. The call includes an artist honorarium and, for designers, participation in a pop-up opportunity to sell pieces.
calls.project_requirements:
The event will take place on Saturday July 4th 2026 at Terms&Conditions: Rue d’Arlon 104, 5th floor. (Brussels, Belgium)
To develop your ceremony/character/… , you are welcome to use one of the teas on the party’s menu as a starting point. This is not a requirement though.
Your pieces will be actively worn by visitors/participants and will be handled with care.

calls.title: Open Call: Abstract – Exhibition, Magazine Feature, Artist Interview
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit work for a virtual exhibition themed around abstraction. Selected artists may also be featured in the magazine and interviewed, with additional promotion through the organisation’s channels. Prizes include a solo show for first prize and a spot in a future group exhibition for second prize.
calls.project_requirements: The Goddessarts Magazine is excited to announce our upcoming theme: Abstract – a celebration of form, color, movement, and emotion. This exhibition invites artists to explore abstraction in all its powerful forms: gestural brushstrokes, geometric clarity, texture-driven work, conceptual abstraction, emotional expression, and beyond. Whether rooted in chaos or calm, minimalism or maximalism, we want to see how abstraction flows through your creative practice. All mediums and styles except video are welcome & everyone is encouraged to apply.

calls.title: Residencies 2027/28
calls.description: The Landis & Gyr Foundation offers artist residencies in Budapest, Bucharest, London, Sofia and Belgrade, as well as Zug residencies for writers and literary translators. The programme provides accommodation and a monthly stipend, and some locations also offer access to studio or rehearsal space. Applicants can choose one location and indicate preferred time periods.
calls.project_requirements: The desired time period (first and second preference) should also be stated.

calls.title: Performing arts: International activities
calls.description: This grant programme supports international performing arts activities linked to performing arts in Denmark and Danish-produced performing arts abroad. It can fund guest performances, touring, site-specific performances, networking, research, workshops, residencies, and other activities that build international collaboration. Grants are available up to DKK 100,000.
calls.project_requirements:
The purpose of the program is to promote performing arts of high artistic quality in Denmark and Danish produced performing arts abroad. We achieve this by supporting internationalization such as:
• International guest performances touring and site specific performances, where an existing concept is adapted to the given context
• Networking and research aimed at long-term international collaborations and co-productions, including participation in workshops abroad as a speaker and the invitation of guests for performances in Denmark
• International residencies
The committee encourages you to incorporate your international activities in your long-term strategic planning, so that your international activities, if possible, are included in larger applications for the funding programme ‘Performing Arts for Children, Young People and Adults’, which has two annual deadlines in January and June. Here you can incorporate your international activities in applications for project grants or as part of your overall seasonal activities.

calls.title: French cultural network residencies around the world
calls.description: This page presents the residency programmes run by the French cultural network abroad. It explains that these residencies support artistic research, experimentation, and professional networking across many creative fields. The page also points to current calls for applications and provides access to the network’s residency map and charter.
calls.project_requirements: A residency is defined by all of the following characteristics: 1. The provision of accommodation and a workspace for the artist. 2. A minimum duration of one month, essential to understanding the local context and to establishing lasting contacts that are relevant to the project, whilst at the same time limiting the residency’s impact on the environment. 3. Administrative, technical, professional and artistic support to encourage research development. 4. A minimum of 70% of the residency time is devoted to the artist's project. 5. The awarding of a residency grant to the artist. Residencies organised within France's cultural network abroad are primarily residencies focusing on creation, research or experimentation. They are not intended to support programmes that are first and foremost geared towards distribution or circulation (touring exhibitions, setting up of exhibitions, participation in symposiums, etc.) or towards training or continuing education, nor are they intended to respond to artistic commissions. Residencies may, however, go hand in hand with other objectives of the post.

calls.title: Independent performing arts – project (theatre)
calls.description: Grants for the artistic production and presentation of theatre, both individual projects and multi-year projects.

calls.title: Performing arts – dance productions
calls.description: Grants for the artistic production and presentation of dance, both single projects and multi-year projects.

calls.title: 5th Medialab Matadero Open Call for the Award of Three (3) Residencies within the Annual Situated Research Programme (2027)
calls.description: This open call offers three seven-month research and creation residencies at Medialab Matadero in Madrid. The residencies support experimental, critical, and collaborative projects at the intersection of contemporary art, design, science, technology, and society. Selected projects will also develop a public programme and take part in a final public showcase.
calls.project_requirements:
The residencies will last for seven (7) months and will take place between January and July 2027.
Submitted projects should engage with Medialab Matadero’s lines of work and operate at the margins or intersections of different disciplines, methodologies, and fields of knowledge.
Projects should adhere to the following guidelines:
• Explore potential intersections between art, design, science, technology, and society.
• Contribute to critical reflection on contemporary socio-technical, cultural, ecological, political, or urban challenges.
• Propose collaborative, experimental, situated, or unconventional research methodologies.
• Establish bonds with communities, agents, collectives, citizen initiatives, professional fields, or bodies of knowledge related to the project.
• Incorporate a public dimension through activities involving learning, dissemination, the exchange of knowledge, mediation, or the presentation of the research process.
As part of the residency, each project must develop a public programme related to its research process.
These may take the form of workshops, encounters, working groups, critical sessions, conversations, open laboratories, presentations, or other platforms for collective experimentation.
Comprising between one and six activities, this public programme will be defined and fine-tuned during the residency in dialogue with the Medialab Matadero team, in accordance with the evolution of the research, the needs of the project, and the availability of spaces and resources.
Furthermore, the selected projects must participate in a final public showcase at Medialab Matadero, scheduled to take place between June and July 2027, where they will share the processes, lessons learnt, methodologies, or findings developed during the residency.

calls.title: Call for Entries
calls.description: This is a call for current works for EMAF in the sections Film, Installation, and Expanded. Selected works can be shown in the festival program and exhibition, with fees/honoraria and invited participation at the festival.
calls.project_requirements: We invite submissions of current works in the sections Film (experimental films of any length and any thematic focus), Installation (installative, interactive, spatial or sculptural media art works) and Expanded (performances, live events or workshops). Submissions for the Installation section should relate to the 2027 festival theme, which will center on the archive – as an instrument of knowledge production, a site of critical intervention and a space for alternative visions of the future. Applications for the Installation and Expanded sections must include a detailed description, tech rider, cost calculation and visual material.

calls.title: Tel Aviv
calls.description: This residency stipend enables artists from North Rhine-Westphalia to spend six months in a live/work studio in Tel Aviv. It is designed to help them get to know the local art scene, build contacts, and develop new approaches in their artistic practice. The residency also aims to support free experimentation and fair working conditions for visual arts residencies abroad.
calls.project_requirements: a six-month stay in a live/work studio in Tel Aviv

calls.title: Art Explora x Cité internationale des arts
calls.organisation: The Art Explora Foundation and the Cité internationale des arts
calls.description: A residency programme for French and international artists and researchers that supports projects engaging with contemporary issues such as new technologies, art and science, and environmental and social questions. It offers two formats: a SOLO programme for artists and a Collective programme for collectives, researchers, and curators. Residents receive studio space, a living allowance, a production grant, and travel to Paris.
calls.project_requirements: The programme invites candidates to propose a project that questions contemporary issues, including new technologies, the links between art and science, and environmental and social issues. Please explain why being based in France is necessary to the development of your project (conceptual, geographical and practical aspects, social ties, etc.).

calls.title: 33rd International Studio Program of the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar OPEN CALL 2026: On Absence
calls.organisation: ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit project proposals for the 33rd International Studio Program in Weimar. The 2026 theme is “On Absence,” and selected artists will take part in an international studio program connected to the ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar.
calls.project_requirements: submit proposals for projects that explore absence and the absent through art, rethink absence in radically new ways, challenge it aesthetically, or use it as a tool for social critique.

calls.title: Open Call for Tokyo Wonder Site residency programs
calls.description: Tokyo Wonder Site Residency offers artist-in-residence programs for international creators in creative fields such as art, design, music and architecture. The page announces two residency programs for 2018: an International Creator Residency Program and a Research Residency Program. The residencies provide time and space for creation and research, along with opportunities to present work and exchange ideas.
calls.project_requirements:
• Residency Period: 3 months
• Residency Period: About 6 weeks

calls.title: Culture and Health
calls.organisation: Ministère de la Culture et ministère de la Santé
calls.description: This programme supports collaborative cultural projects in healthcare and medico-social settings. It is organized regionally and can take the form of artist residencies or other regional calls, bringing together cultural actors, artists, and health institutions to develop participatory artistic actions for patients, residents, families, and staff.
calls.project_requirements:
Projects must take place over a period between 1 June 2026 and 30 June 2027.
The Regional Directorate of Cultural Affairs, the Regional Health Agency and the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur Region are rolling out Culture and Health 2025 in the form of artist residencies for creation and transmission, promoting participatory artistic and cultural approaches led by artists.
This format of intervention makes it possible to present artistic proposals to audiences through residencies of at least six weeks (consecutive or not) within structures (hospital, nursing home, health centre, etc.). The approach includes creation periods and transmission periods with audiences.
All artistic fields are concerned: live performance (theatre, music, dance, circus, street art, etc.) visual arts, graphic arts, cinema, books and reading, museums, digital practices, etc.
The projects must be carried out during the 2026 calendar year.
Artistic and cultural projects co-built between three partners will be supported: at minimum a health establishment, a cultural facility and one or more qualified professional artists.
In order to help a larger number of establishments, projects allowing cooperation between several health establishments will be appreciated.
The actions must allow both:
• access to works,
• artistic practice,
• sharing around know-how,
• transmission of cultural knowledge.
Because of the audiences reached, and because time is needed to foster the encounter, the projects must provide for a minimum of 25 hours of artistic intervention with the participating people (excluding dissemination, preparation and meetings).
These projects may be multidisciplinary. They may propose actions in all artistic fields, books and reading, heritage, social sciences, architecture, scientific culture.
The following cannot be supported:
• animation projects and educational actions.
• art therapy workshops.
• artistic mediation with a relational purpose such as forum theatre or relational clowning.
• actions led by associations working in hospitals, whose very purpose is artistic intervention with hospitalised people.
• actions relating solely to communication, training or prevention objectives.
• projects consisting solely of programming performances, concerts, exhibitions.
• isolated initiatives designed by one department for one department.
• actions included in the institution’s operations.
• projects aimed solely at staff participation.
• public procurement procedures or the 1% artistic scheme.

calls.title: 2027 DancEUA Artist-in-Residence
calls.description: An international artist-in-residence opportunity for dance professionals within the DancEUA project. It offers residency time, studio access, mentoring, and a work-in-progress presentation in Sweden. The program is aimed at developing new work or further developing an existing dance or performing arts production.
calls.project_requirements:
looking to create a new work or further develop an existing dance or performing arts production.
Dance professionals working on solo or duet projects.
The program culminates in a work-in-progress presentation, allowing artists to share their artistic works with the local audience of Tanum.

statement:
I am an illustrator and comics artist. I make graphic novels, picture books and editorial illustration, drawing by hand and digitally. My stories are about childhood, migration and everyday life.

I am looking for comics and illustration residencies, grants for graphic novels and picture books, illustration competitions, and publishing opportunities.

calls.title: Things that do not sell (‘Stuff that does not sell’)
calls.description: This open call invites visual artists to submit small works for a group exhibition in Antwerp that explores the friction between truth and make-believe. Selected works will be shown in a temporary “department store” format during the exhibition period in December 2025. The call focuses on objects, editions, multiples, zines, and other publication forms that tell a false or distorted narrative.
calls.project_requirements: We are looking for unique objects and/or editions/multiples that tell a false or distorted narrative through text or image. Three-dimensional works and objects, as well as zines and alternative forms of publication, are eligible. We prefer objects that can be displayed on a shelf, newspaper carousel, or table. Works intended for wall mounting are not eligible. Specifics: Your work tells a (fictional) story through text and/or image. We are looking for small works: you can hold them in one hand and they cost no more than €100 (including VAT).

calls.title: Artist Project
calls.description: The Artist Project grant supports visual artists who want to realise a concrete artistic plan within a defined working period. It can cover project costs for new work, collaboration, travel, research, mentoring, or a residency in the Netherlands or abroad. The grant is intended to help artists develop work that can strengthen the quality and visibility of contemporary visual art.
calls.project_requirements: To implement a specific plan, tied to a clear working period. It can also involve collaboration. The grant is to help cover project costs, such as the execution of a concrete plan for new work, a collaboration, a period of travel or a working period. It may also entail research, mentoring or a stay at a residency in the Netherlands or abroad. The duration of the contribution must be justified by a global timeline, included in your plan. Applicants are obliged to contribute at least 10% of the total sum being requested from the Mondriaan Fund. This can be in the form of a personal investment, contributions from third parties, an interest-free loan from Fonds Kwadraat or a contribution raised through crowdfunding. This means that the contribution from the Mondriaan Fund will be for a maximum of 90% of the costs that are eligible for the grant. If the application involves another party, such as an art venue, museum, gallery, company or client, the financial contribution from this party must be in acceptable proportion to the contribution requested from the Mondriaan Fund. Cultural institutions are expected to subscribe to the Fair Practice Code. Compliance with the Fair Practice Code automatically means that the institution implements the Guideline for Artists’ Fees. What is eligible: The cost of materials specifically related to the project. Rental of equipment and materials. If equipment is purchased that is strictly necessary for the project, the depreciation costs can be included in the budget. Travel expenses for a return flight, train journey or mileage allowance to and from the main location as stated in the application. Local travel expenses are part of the contribution covering time investment. Hiring third parties (including travel and accommodation expenses, if applicable). Residency expenses: Please note that the contribution covering time investment is halved if a residency fee is included in the budget, or if it becomes apparent that the residency covers the following expenses: accommodation and meals. In the case of an artist’s book, the contribution may only be used for a special publication that can be considered an autonomous work of art in its own right and is produced in an edition of no more than 3 copies. The Artist Project grant may not be used for other publications, but the Publication grant is available for such projects. What is not eligible: Regular expenses, such as ongoing housing costs and child care are not eligible for a grant. The grant is not intended for work for an organisation, for regular work activities, exhibition costs or other costs of presenting work. The grant cannot be used to put previously produced work back into production, to frame work or transfer it to a different medium. Costs associated with a stay abroad and that are covered by the contribution for time investment include accommodation, meals and local travel expenses. An application can be made for these costs for third parties involved with the project. The Artist Project grant may not be used for a working period in a guest studio in the Netherlands or abroad if this studio is offered in the Mondriaan Fund’s Residency The Artist Project grant may not be used for activities or a project at institutions/art venues receiving long-term financial support from one of the Rijkscultuurfondsen (public cultural funds) or the Basic Cultural Infrastructure (BIS), unless it concerns non-standard programming.

calls.title: Apply for artist-in-residence
calls.description: Konstepidemin offers international guest studios for artists to live and work in Gothenburg. The residency includes a studio space, bedroom, kitchen and bathroom, and artists also get access to shared facilities such as a printer/scanner/copy machine and a graphics workshop. Applications are accepted throughout the year for stays of one to six months.
calls.project_requirements: Konstepidemin’s five guest studios can be rented for periods of one to six months, and a minimum of one month is required. Please plan ahead and make sure to apply with some flexibility regarding your desired dates for residency. Longer periods are prioritized.

calls.title: International Art Presentation
calls.description: This grant supports artists and internationally recognised art institutions for presentations of contemporary visual art abroad. It can cover visibility-related costs and, in some cases, the production of new work. Applications are accepted continuously through an online system.
calls.project_requirements:
Costs that increase the visibility of the work and for the production of new work.
If the application relates to the production of new work, the international institution is expected to include a realistic fee for the artist in the budget, with an explanation of how the amount of the fee was determined.
It is also possible to apply together with other artists, although the application must involve a joint plan that leads to a shared result.
In the case of a joint exhibition, all participants are required to submit a separate application form.

calls.title: Work and Research Grants
calls.description: This call offers work and research fellowships for individual artistic approaches in visual art for up to 12 months in Germany or abroad. It provides monthly support for research and work projects, with a separate track for international stays that also covers travel costs.
calls.project_requirements:
We award work and research grants for individual artistic approaches of up to 12 months for Germany and abroad.
For further projects (productions, publications, other formats, etc.), a prior consultation and the submission of a written interim report are mandatory.

calls.title: Art Residency Program
calls.description: Can Serrat offers an international art residency program for writers and contemporary artists from around the world. The program provides short- and medium-term residencies with time, space, follow-up, individual and collective support, and a professional network. Some calls include full grants and partial grants.
calls.project_requirements: There is no expectation of a finished product at the end of the residency, and the program does not aim to organize gallery exhibitions.

calls.title: Apply for residency
calls.description: This is a residency opportunity at the Danish Art Workshops for professional artists, designers, craftspeople and art restorers who need access to large-format workshops and facilities. It offers studio and workshop access, accommodation in a guest flat, and consultation, with projects in either development/research or production/completion. Residencies can support work for exhibition, decoration, or other cultural activity in Denmark.
calls.project_requirements:
• DEVELOPMENT Projects deriving from material based, artistic development / research including material research, prototype production or other kinds of “work in process”.
• Projects that resemble research, exploration, and innovation.
• The purpose of the project must be well described.
• PRODUCTION Projects, that focus on production and completion of works for exhibition, decoration etc.
• It may be single works or a full exhibition.
• Projects targeted a public review in- or outside of Denmark.
• You can apply for a residency of up to six months.
• The length of the residency has to fit your project.
• Please state if you are flexible on the exact period of time or the studio you have applied for.
• In some cases, the committee assesses that a project can be done in a shorter period of time and this might result in a shorter term of residency, than was applied for.

calls.title: Different art forms
calls.description: This funding page explains how to apply when an artistic project combines different art forms or does not fit neatly into one category. It supports artistic work that breaks with traditional genres or is hard to define, and it may be assessed by more than one committee if relevant. Applicants are guided on whether to submit one application or split a project into separate subprojects across different funding programmes.
calls.project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.
When you break down your project into several applications, it is important that you also split up your budget, since you are not able to get the same expenses covered by more than one funding programme.
Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.
In some cases, two or more committees join together to fund a grant.
This will often happen, if a project’s budget is too large for one committee to fund it all.

calls.title: Open Call: Abstract – Exhibition, Magazine Feature, Artist Interview
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit work for a virtual exhibition themed around abstraction. Selected artists may also be featured in the magazine and interviewed, with additional promotion through the organisation’s channels. Prizes include a solo show for first prize and a spot in a future group exhibition for second prize.
calls.project_requirements: The Goddessarts Magazine is excited to announce our upcoming theme: Abstract – a celebration of form, color, movement, and emotion. This exhibition invites artists to explore abstraction in all its powerful forms: gestural brushstrokes, geometric clarity, texture-driven work, conceptual abstraction, emotional expression, and beyond. Whether rooted in chaos or calm, minimalism or maximalism, we want to see how abstraction flows through your creative practice. All mediums and styles except video are welcome & everyone is encouraged to apply.

calls.title: Application for General Projects
calls.description: This funding call supports general visual arts projects such as exhibitions, new productions, publications, and acquisitions for a museum collection. It is part of the Visual Arts programme of Kunststiftung NRW and is aimed at professional artists and institutions/initiatives from North Rhine-Westphalia. Applications are submitted through the application portal, with deadlines twice a year.
calls.project_requirements:
We support, for example, exhibitions, new productions, publications and acquisitions into the collection holdings of a museum.
We do not support database development, database maintenance, acquisition of technical infrastructure, the creation of digitized copies, documentation, prizes, projects from archaeology, or cultural education.

calls.title: Seeking Support
calls.description: DGARTES presents open funding opportunities for artistic activity through its support programmes and funding lines. The page points applicants to the candidate support area and the management platform where application forms are available. It also links to the annual declaration listing the open calls and funding amounts for 2026.

calls.title: Residency in Berlin, Bethanien
calls.organisation: The Swedish Arts Grants Committee’s International Programme for Visual and Applied Artists, IASPIS
calls.description: This residency programme offers artists a studio, housing, and a stipend for a stay at Künstlerhaus Bethanien in Berlin. It is intended to support artists’ opportunities to create, develop, and build contacts outside Sweden. The residency runs in collaboration with Künstlerhaus Bethanien, a studio programme and project workshop for international contemporary art.

calls.title: Artists‘ Salary Fund
calls.description: The Artists‘ Salary Fund is a funding opportunity for artists working in Iceland. It supports artistic practice through salary funding decided by the yearly budget of the parliament, and it can also apply travel grants.

calls.title: Visual art – publications and manuscript development
calls.description: Support for producing or disseminating art professional publications, or for developing manuscripts about visual contemporary art.

calls.title: Artist Basic
calls.description: Artist Basic is a grant for visual artists to support the development of their professional practice and the creation of new work. It offers funding that can be used for research, experimentation, materials or equipment, commissions, and participation in exhibitions or events. The grant is intended to help artists expand their oeuvre, visibility, and cultural entrepreneurship.
calls.project_requirements:
For creating work.
That can include research, experimentation, or the purchase of new materials or equipment. Or it can help with the execution of a commission and/or participation in exhibitions or events in the Netherlands or abroad.

calls.title: Hessische Kulturstiftung 2027/2028 travel and residency grants
calls.description: This call offers travel grants, residency grants, and combined residency and travel grants for visual artists. It supports artistic work over several months in destinations such as New York City, London, Paris, Istanbul, and Kyoto, with additional funding available for production or presentation of works. Applications are submitted through the application portal on the page.
calls.project_requirements: For the years 2027 and 2028, the Hessische Kulturstiftung will award altogether 5 travel grants of 3 to 12 months duration for destinations of the recipient’s choice, 7 residency grants of up to 12 months duration (New York City, London, Cité internationale des arts in Paris: 12 months, Istanbul: 6 months), and 2 combined residency and travel grants (residency at the Goethe-Institut Villa Kamogawa in Kyoto: 3 months, followed by an individual travel and work phase: 3 months).

calls.title: Support for the publication of books in Icelandic
calls.description: This is a funding scheme that provides temporary financial aid to publishers for the publication of books in Icelandic. It reimburses part of eligible publication costs, including labour, printing, translation, proofreading, and promotion. Applications are submitted electronically through the application system.
calls.project_requirements:
The published book must be in Icelandic.
Eligible expenses incurred in the publication of the book and for which the applicant requests support must amount to at least ISK 1 million. Lower thresholds for books published on digital media and for certain classes of books may be laid down in a Regulation.
Costs incurred in the publication of a book intended primarily as a means of promoting a particular product or service do not qualify as eligible expenses under this Act.

calls.title: Art Media
calls.description: The Art Media grant supports written and/or spoken word publications that stimulate engagement with and discourse on contemporary visual art. It is aimed at projects such as article series, long reads and podcasts published on public media or online platforms. The grant can support individual practitioners or organisations working in this field, with the amount determined per application based on the budget.
calls.project_requirements: For written and/or spoken word publications. Applications can be submitted for e.g. a series of articles, long reads and podcasts that are published in/on (online) magazines, newspapers, social media channels or other online platforms. The planned publication must be accessible on at least one public medium or platform with appropriate reach. The project may not be directly linked to the applicant’s existing activities (e.g. an article or publication accompanying an exhibition). It is not possible to apply for a grant for television or film productions. It is not possible to apply for a grant for making profiles or portraits of artists.

calls.title: Creative Steps for Individuals
calls.description: Creative Steps for Individuals is a funding opportunity for artists and creative professionals in Wales who have experienced barriers to careers within the arts. It supports professional, business and organisational development rather than the creation of new work. Applicants can use the grant for activities such as mentoring, training, networking, business development, website development, or setting up a new organisation.
calls.project_requirements: Creative Steps for Individuals is for supporting career development, and NOT for creating new work or project delivery. Please bear in mind that you need to allow a minimum of 12 working weeks between the deadline date and the start date of your project. We cannot fund proposals that are already happening so we won’t accept your application if your proposal’s start date will come before we’ve had the opportunity to assess your application.

calls.title: Artist Start
calls.description: Artist Start is a grant for visual artists at the beginning of their professional careers. It supports the development of their art practice and cultural entrepreneurship, including making work, research, experimentation, and presenting work in exhibitions or events. The grant provides funding for 12 months.
calls.project_requirements: You can use this grant to develop your art practice. That can include making work, research, experimentation, the purchase of materials and equipment, and so on. Or it could be used for working on a commission or participating in exhibitions or events at home or abroad.

calls.title: THE ARTIST PRIZE 2027
calls.description: An open call competition for artists to submit artworks for the BBA Artist Prize 2027. Selected artists can be included in a shortlist and show their work in an exhibition in Berlin, with prizes and online promotion awarded to winners. The call welcomes all mediums and all themes.
calls.project_requirements:
Submit up to 5 artworks - this entitles you to be eligible for the long and shortlist and show your art at our exclusive exhibition in Berlin.
All themes welcome -

calls.title: Visual art – production and dissemination – exhibition venues
calls.description: Grants to produce and disseminate visual art.

calls.title: International Support for Galleries and Independent Exhibition Spaces
calls.organisation: OCA – Office for Contemporary Art Norway on behalf of OCA and Norwegian Crafts (NC)
calls.description: This is a grant scheme that supports Norway-based galleries, independent exhibition spaces, and art book publishers taking part in international art fairs. It helps cover participation costs such as fair fees, transport, insurance, and travel/accommodation for staff and artists. Applications are processed in rounds throughout the year until the budget is exhausted.
calls.project_requirements:
Applicants must present at least one Norwegian or Norway-based contemporary artist at one of the international art fairs included in the list of eligible art fairs.
Applicants must present at least three publications about or featuring Norwegian or Norway-based contemporary artists at one of the international art book fairs included in the list of eligible art fairs.
Of these publications, at least three must be registered with an ISBN.
Applications must be submitted before the fair opens.
The project has opened or been finalised before the deadline for the application round.

calls.title: Building and infrastructure - ARENA Grant for building and infrastructure measures in the arts and culture field
calls.description: This is a funding opportunity for building and infrastructure projects in the arts and culture field. It supports new builds, renovations, upgrades, feasibility studies, and pilot projects for professional arts and culture arenas and infrastructure across Norway. The scheme is intended to strengthen sustainable spaces and infrastructure for production, presentation, and professional development.
calls.project_requirements: The arena or infrastructure you are applying for funding for must be used for professional arts and cultural activity, or for collaboration between professional and voluntary arts and cultural life. The project you are applying for funding for must benefit the arts and culture fields and/or a general audience. The Arts Council assumes that the project is carried out in accordance with public law. We do not provide funding for developing arenas for private business activity and premises that are only to be rented out on commercial terms pure production or workshop premises that are only accessible to individual artists or a smaller group of artists/actors enterprises where public debt negotiations or bankruptcy proceedings have been opened ordinary operations to buy buildings or property to buy personal equipment, supplies, consumables or artworks to buy equipment for the purpose of (commercial) rental activities scenography or decoration kitchen and catering facilities measures that belong under other grant schemes in the Arts Council

calls.title: Application form – studio at Konstepidemin
calls.description: Konstepidemin is accepting applications for a studio space at its art center in Gothenburg. The form asks applicants to indicate their preferred studio size and area of interest, and it also notes community duties connected to being an artist at Konstepidemin. Applicants must submit a CV and a personal letter describing their practice and why they want a studio there.
calls.project_requirements: As an artist at Konstepidemin you are required to take part in the board, the culture committee, or one of our work sections: gallery, studio, stage, kids and youths, the international group, outdoor/gardening. Check area of interest (more than one is allowed).

calls.title: Silent Book Contest 2027 – Gianni De Conno Award
calls.description: An international contest for illustrated books without words. It invites artists to submit unpublished book projects that tell a story entirely through illustrations, with the winning project published by Carthusia Edizioni and awarded a cash prize. Finalists will also be exhibited at the Bologna Children’s Book Fair 2027, and there is a Junior Prize linked to school-age readers.
calls.project_requirements: The competition is exclusively reserved for new and unpublished illustrated books without words. The subject is open and not restricted to any age group and readers. The narration must be carried out exclusively through illustrated images and have narrative and stylistic coherence. The book projects entered in the competition must be sent anonymously following the instructions given in the section “On-line registration procedure for submitting material”. Book projects submitted and not corresponding to the Participation Methods or incomplete book projects will not be admitted. Also books already published in Italy and other countries won’t be admitted.

calls.title: Art Explora x Cité internationale des arts
calls.organisation: The Art Explora Foundation and the Cité internationale des arts
calls.description: A residency programme for French and international artists and researchers that supports projects engaging with contemporary issues such as new technologies, art and science, and environmental and social questions. It offers two formats: a SOLO programme for artists and a Collective programme for collectives, researchers, and curators. Residents receive studio space, a living allowance, a production grant, and travel to Paris.
calls.project_requirements: The programme invites candidates to propose a project that questions contemporary issues, including new technologies, the links between art and science, and environmental and social issues. Please explain why being based in France is necessary to the development of your project (conceptual, geographical and practical aspects, social ties, etc.).

calls.title: Create and Engage
calls.description: Create and Engage funds the development, creation and delivery of high-quality arts experiences that help creative individuals and organisations engage with and connect to the public. It supports projects involving creation, presentation, programming, touring, community participation, and training and professional development for organisations. There are two levels of award, and projects must align with the fund’s priorities and supported artforms.
calls.project_requirements: Applications must be focussed on the artforms that we support. Your project must take place mainly in Wales. We can only fund activities or events taking place outside of Wales where you can demonstrate longer-term benefit to individuals and communities within Wales. We can consider funding some international activity as part of a wider project if a clear rationale is given. Your project must complement and enhance your usual programme of activity. This means it should not be part of your core activity or include core costs. Your proposal should be for new activity, or work linked to an upcoming opportunity (such as a specific commission, collaboration, presentation, development period, or public engagement activity). Your project must involve working with others. Your project must be time limited. This means it has a definite start and end date. You must have other funding to contribute to the overall costs of your project. You must allow adequate lead time.

statement:
I am an architect and designer working at the edge of art and architecture. I make spatial installations, temporary pavilions and research on sustainable materials such as timber, earth and reuse. My projects deal with housing, ecology and the commons.

I am looking for design and architecture competitions, grants for spatial and design research, and residencies for architects and designers.

calls.title: IV INVITATION TO PARTICIPATE IN THE SELECTION OF THREE SITUATED RESEARCH PROJECTS AS PART OF THE ANNUAL MEDIALAB MATADERO PROGRAM AT MATADERO MADRID 2025-2026
calls.organisation: Medialab Matadero / Matadero Madrid / Madrid Destino, Cultura, Turismo y Negocio S.A.
calls.description: This invitation selects three situated research projects for the 2025-2026 annual program at Medialab Matadero in Matadero Madrid. The selected projects will be developed over up to one year and will engage with Medialab Matadero’s activities and communities. The program supports collaborative, experimental research at the intersection of art, design, science, technology, and society.
calls.project_requirements: Submitted projects must adhere to a series of fundamental guidelines: Thematic coherence. In general terms, projects should explore the possible intersections between art, design, science and technology and their results or methods should creatively contribute to addressing major contemporary urban and global challenges within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals of the 2030 Agenda. In particular, all submitted projects should engage with the lines of work of Medialab Matadero, which include all the themes addressed in the annual programmes Lab 1: Sentient Media, Lab 2: The Metabolic Sublime, Lab 3: Synthetic Minds and Lab 4: Weird Futures, with the aim of updating and further exploring the lines of research opened up by Medialab in recent years. Innovation and critical reflection. Developing a cultural project of critical reflection that contributes to a better digital future, tracking the digital revolution at all scales and its impact on society. Dialogue. The project must be able to engage in dialogue with the rest of Medialab’s activities. It should also be capable of transformation and enrichment through this dialogue in contact with partners (individuals and other organisations), other researchers, users, and the public. Initiation of the research process: Carry out documentation tasks, as well as activities relating to learning, dissemination and public feedback. When the research is complete, an event must be held at Matadero to present the findings.

calls.title: Residency in Berlin, Bethanien
calls.organisation: The Swedish Arts Grants Committee’s International Programme for Visual and Applied Artists, IASPIS
calls.description: This residency programme offers artists a studio, housing, and a stipend for a stay at Künstlerhaus Bethanien in Berlin. It is intended to support artists’ opportunities to create, develop, and build contacts outside Sweden. The residency runs in collaboration with Künstlerhaus Bethanien, a studio programme and project workshop for international contemporary art.

calls.title: 5th Medialab Matadero Open Call for the Award of Three (3) Residencies within the Annual Situated Research Programme (2027)
calls.description: This open call offers three seven-month research and creation residencies at Medialab Matadero in Madrid. The residencies support experimental, critical, and collaborative projects at the intersection of contemporary art, design, science, technology, and society. Selected projects will also develop a public programme and take part in a final public showcase.
calls.project_requirements:
The residencies will last for seven (7) months and will take place between January and July 2027.
Submitted projects should engage with Medialab Matadero’s lines of work and operate at the margins or intersections of different disciplines, methodologies, and fields of knowledge.
Projects should adhere to the following guidelines:
• Explore potential intersections between art, design, science, technology, and society.
• Contribute to critical reflection on contemporary socio-technical, cultural, ecological, political, or urban challenges.
• Propose collaborative, experimental, situated, or unconventional research methodologies.
• Establish bonds with communities, agents, collectives, citizen initiatives, professional fields, or bodies of knowledge related to the project.
• Incorporate a public dimension through activities involving learning, dissemination, the exchange of knowledge, mediation, or the presentation of the research process.
As part of the residency, each project must develop a public programme related to its research process.
These may take the form of workshops, encounters, working groups, critical sessions, conversations, open laboratories, presentations, or other platforms for collective experimentation.
Comprising between one and six activities, this public programme will be defined and fine-tuned during the residency in dialogue with the Medialab Matadero team, in accordance with the evolution of the research, the needs of the project, and the availability of spaces and resources.
Furthermore, the selected projects must participate in a final public showcase at Medialab Matadero, scheduled to take place between June and July 2027, where they will share the processes, lessons learnt, methodologies, or findings developed during the residency.

calls.title: Individual Project Architecture
calls.organisation: Bundesministerium für Wohnen, Kunst, Kultur, Medien und Sport, Sektion IV Kunst und Kultur, Abteilung IV/B/4 – Architektur, Baukultur, Denkmalschutz und UNESCO-Welterbe
calls.description: This call supports individual architecture-related projects, exhibitions, publications, and travel or transport costs. It provides partial funding for projects in Austria and abroad, with applications submitted through an online funding form.
calls.project_requirements:
Applications must be submitted no later than 3 months before the project start date.
Projects that pursue a purely commercial intention are not recommended for funding, as well as projects (exhibitions, publications, etc.) in commercial Austrian galleries/institutions, participation in trade fairs
Projects by persons still in training are not recommended for funding, as well as projects by universities or projects within the framework of university studies
Projects or undertakings that are part of already funded annual programs or projects cannot be recommended for funding
Funding for projects, exhibitions in/from Austrian territorial authorities and their institutions cannot be funded, likewise scholarship programs of the Austrian federal states are not supported. Events of the federal museums also do not fall within the responsibility of the department.
There is no responsibility on the part of the department for the funding of structural renovation and adaptation work, studio conversions

calls.title: Competition 2026 – Designing a space of impulse and resonance in the church interior
calls.description: This is an open, anonymous design competition for a permanent artistic intervention in the church St. Dionysius in Nordwalde. It invites contemporary concepts that create an impulse and resonance space in the church interior and engage with themes of participation, vocation, proclamation, and responsibility, especially in relation to Mary Magdalene. The winning proposal is intended for realization in the church and is supported by the parish and the ars LITURGICA initiative.
calls.project_requirements:
This is an open and anonymous competition. A design is to be submitted in accordance with the design task described above for the parish church of St. Dionysius in Nordwalde. A high artistic quality as well as liturgical sensitivity are expected.
Scale, materiality and placement must be matched to the architecture of the church. Techniques and materials are freely selectable (painting, sculpture, relief, installation, light art …).
The work is to be conceived for a permanent installation in the church space.
It must therefore be taken into account,
• that the work and spatial design to be realized later take into consideration the liturgical practices customary on site and the pastoral work
• and that the area designated for the design is prominently located in the line of sight of the two main entrances to the church space.
The competition entries submitted may not be copies of other works. They may not yet have been submitted to other competitions or published in relevant publications.

calls.title: THE SWISS ATELIER @ 3daysofdesign 2027
calls.description: THE SWISS ATELIER is an open call for projects to be presented at 3daysofdesign 2027 in the Swiss Embassy in Copenhagen. It offers selected designers, brands and design schools the chance to create spatial proposals for three different rooms within the embassy. The call focuses on innovative materials, responsible production, craftsmanship and new approaches to everyday life.
calls.project_requirements:
We only accept proposals within the fields of furniture, interior design, lighting, lifestyle concepts, and/or experimental architecture.
Applicants must submit a developed concept, including the creative direction, spatial approach, and the works, objects or elements that will form part of the experience.
The proposal can take many forms, from an immersive installation or curated environment to a new collaboration or unexpected interpretation of the space.
The selected works should feel as though they belong there while bringing something unexpected to the space.
Its placement, relationship with the existing furniture and surroundings, and the story it introduces can all become part of the proposal.

calls.title: Call for collaborators for the collaborative prototyping laboratory LAB 4 Weird Futures
calls.description: LAB 4 Weird Futures is a multidisciplinary research and collaborative production programme at Medialab Matadero Madrid. calls.title: Proud architecture: open call for LGBTQIA+ architects
calls.description: RIBA is inviting LGBTQIA+ architects to submit work for a new exhibition celebrating contemporary architectural practice. • education
• healthcare
• workplaces and commercial projects
• cultural and community buildings
• civic architecture
• public realm
• retrofit, restoration, and reuse
• temporary or experimental architecture
• smaller-scale projects and interventions

calls.title: Apply for artist-in-residence
calls.description: Konstepidemin offers international guest studios for artists to live and work in Gothenburg. calls.title: Building and infrastructure - ARENA Grant for building and infrastructure measures in the arts and culture field
calls.description: This is a funding opportunity for building and infrastructure projects in the arts and culture field. The scheme is intended to strengthen sustainable spaces and infrastructure for production, presentation, and professional development.
calls.project_requirements: The arena or infrastructure you are applying for funding for must be used for professional arts and cultural activity, or for collaboration between professional and voluntary arts and cultural life. The project you are applying for funding for must benefit the arts and culture fields and/or a general audience.
