calls.title: Improvement of the material and technical base of design and architecture educational institutions
calls.description: This is a funding call for projects that improve the material and technical base of design and architecture educational institutions. It is part of VKKF’s regular project competitions and is administered through the VKKF project application system. The page links to the competition regulations and the application system.

calls.title: Research and Development
calls.description: Research and Development supports the development and creation of high-quality and ambitious work. It helps applicants explore new ideas and ways of working with partners, with funding available at two levels: small and large. The project should be aimed at reaching audiences and showing strong potential for future success.
calls.project_requirements:
Proposals should have a clear intention to create work that will reach audiences and demonstrate a strong potential for future success. Small Research & Development can explore how a new idea can become a developed product. It can give you time and space to pursue new concepts and take you beyond your usual creative practice. You should have partners committed to supporting your idea and show that their experience and involvement is appropriate at this stage. Be clear if you expect your work to be audience ready at the end of the term and if so, how you will ensure this. Consider how you’ll share your work in progress with the people and organisations you need onboard to take the project to realisation. Large Research & Development can be for development of works of larger scale or complexity or can build on a previous research and product development phase. If it is a first development stage, be clear on why a larger investment is necessary. Please include information on how the process will be shared and with who, for example details of any sharings and potential partners or stakeholders needed to support the work to its realisation. If this is a further development phase, it should lead to a product being ready to reach its audience. At this stage, you should have clear plans for presenting the work and should have developed audience and marketing plans. You can apply for a maximum of two research and development grants per work . You need to evidence why a further stage is needed and that it will be ‘audience ready’ at the end of this term. We accept Research and Development projects focussed on the artforms that we support . Your project will take place mostly in Wales , aiming to provide new and exciting experiences for audiences here. Your project must complement and enhance your usual programme of activity . This means it should not be part of your core activity or include core costs. This is particularly the case with Multi-Year Funded Organisations. Your project must involve working with others . The best projects happen when partners are involved. We’ll expect to see you working with at least one other individual or organisation who’ll support you to develop and deliver your project. This could be:
• a partner organisation
• artistic collaborator
• critical friend
• artistic mentor
Your partners can bring different skills and expertise to the proposal, to support you to realise your ambition for the work to be seen, to be relevant and reach its audience. Your project must be time limited . This means it has a definite start and end date. You must have other funding to contribute to the overall costs of your project . We can only support 90% of the project costs. At least 10% of your project income should come from a non-Arts Council or National Lottery source. This other funding can include Support in Kind, and there is no limit on Support in Kind. You must allow adequate lead in time . We’ll expect to see sufficient time built into your project to deliver the work effectively. This is particularly important when it comes to any audience development, outreach or sharing of work.

calls.title: Open Call for Tokyo Wonder Site residency programs
calls.description: Tokyo Wonder Site Residency offers artist-in-residence programs for international creators in creative fields such as art, design, music and architecture. The page announces two residency programs for 2018: an International Creator Residency Program and a Research Residency Program. calls.title: Kunsthaus am Wald International Artist in Residence Program Weitenhagen/ Germany

The location is remote, and site-specific projects are welcome but not required.
calls.project_requirements: Site-specific projects that engage with the spatial context are welcome, though they are not a mandatory requirement for a residency stay.

calls.title: Open Call 2027: Urban Ecologies: Coexistence and Control
calls.description: Lendhauer invites artists and interdisciplinary practitioners to develop projects for Klagenfurt’s Lendhafen around the theme “Urban Ecologies: Coexistence and Control.” The selected works will be realized in the public space and should engage with the site’s social, ecological, and material conditions. The call supports the development and presentation of site-specific artistic projects in 2027.
calls.project_requirements: Artworks are sought that will be realised in the Klagenfurter Lendhafen and engage with the social, ecological and material conditions of public space. The urban space is understood not only as a place of presentation, but as an active component of the work. The selected works will be realised between early June and the end of September 2027. The exact timing and duration depend on the nature and requirements of the respective project and will be determined together with the selected persons.

calls.title: Craft and design projects in Denmark and abroad
calls.description: This funding programme supports projects for and with Danish craft and design in Denmark and abroad. It can support exhibitions, dissemination, residencies, exchange/work stays, production of works, and other project formats within the craft and design field. The programme also includes support for fees and, in some cases, exhibition remuneration.
calls.project_requirements:
You cannot receive funding for:
• Activities completed before the application deadline
• Courses of study/training courses
• Projects that the committee have previously supported
• Capital investments and operating expenses
• Expenses from previous calendar years. That is, only expenses from either the same or upcoming calendar year can be entered into the budget

What is a project? A project is characterised by having an intention; a project has a time limitation and has a target group. This means that you must be able to define your project with a goal, an intention, a schedule, a budget, a target group or audience and any partners.

The committee wants to award grants to projects that are characterised by good and original ideas, are realistic, achievable and, not least, that create meaning for relevant target groups.

The Committee funds projects of high artistic quality throughout the entire craft and design field and is aware that craft and design is a broad practise. The Committee looks for projects that demonstrate aesthetic potential and a keen understanding of the craft, its materials and sensuousness, as well as projects centered on specific design solutions to specific problems or projects of a more intangible nature.

calls.title: Residencies / Biodesign Research Residency / BIZIRIK / EKHŌ / BILME
calls.description: The Basque Biodesign Center offers several research residencies focused on biodesign, biofashion, and textile innovation. Residents get access to specialized labs, machinery, technical and teaching support, and a collaborative environment to develop concepts, prototypes, and sustainable materials. The program connects design, technology, craft, and local resources, with residencies aimed at emerging creators as well as experienced textile practitioners.
calls.project_requirements:
Design and innovation for the development of new uses with local waste will be the axis of the project. The main goal of biodesign research residency is to develop new sustainable products, new materials as a way to transform, revaluate and unite rural and urban lifestyles using local raw materials.

The main goal of this residency is to empower experienced professionals to push the boundaries of digital jacquard design in order to develop new sustainable textile structures and alternatives. We seek to transform the fashion industry by bridging cutting-edge technology with the use of novel materials, upcycling local resources, and connecting artisanal heritage with the design of the future.

calls.title: OPEN CALL FOR PROJECTS LAB 4 WEIRD FUTURES

statement:

I am looking for textile and craft residencies, grants for artists working with traditional techniques, and exhibitions of contemporary textile art.

For creating work.

Applications are submitted through the application portal, with deadlines twice a year.
calls.project_requirements:
We support, for example, exhibitions, new productions, publications and acquisitions into the collection holdings of a museum.
We do not support database development, database maintenance, acquisition of technical infrastructure, the creation of digitized copies, documentation, prizes, projects from archaeology, or cultural education.

calls.title: Contemporary Talents Competition: Water – Wattwiller
calls.description: This is an international contemporary art competition focused on the theme of water. The Foundation acquires selected works, awards prizes to the laureates, and presents the winning artists in an exhibition at its art centre in Wattwiller. Artists may apply with an existing work, and in some cases sculpture or installation projects to be produced.

The work submitted must be on the theme of Water.

calls.title: Residency in Berlin, Bethanien

calls.title: Different art forms

calls.project_requirements:
If your application primarily concerns one specific art form and only to a lesser extent includes others, you should only submit one application.
If your project combines two or more different art forms on equal terms, you may split up your project into separate subprojects and submit separate applications for each subproject to different funding programmes.

Additionally, you must remember to state clearly that you have applied for funding from other programmes within the Danish Arts Foundation, with applications relating to other parts of your projects.
If you find it difficult to split up your project, you have to decide on a programme that you submit one application to, which covers the entire project.

This is developed together with the curators present, who are also responsible for implementation.
In the working duo with the curator present at the same time, two projects are generally to be realized independently for changing cooperation venues.

As part of the residency, each project must develop a public programme related to its research process.
These may take the form of workshops, encounters, working groups, critical sessions, conversations, open laboratories, presentations, or other platforms for collective experimentation.
Comprising between one and six activities, this public programme will be defined and fine-tuned during the residency in dialogue with the Medialab Matadero team, in accordance with the evolution of the research, the needs of the project, and the availability of spaces and resources.
Furthermore, the selected projects must participate in a final public showcase at Medialab Matadero, scheduled to take place between June and July 2027, where they will share the processes, lessons learnt, methodologies, or findings developed during the residency.

calls.title: BIEN Textile Art Biennial Slovenia 2027: Traces of Grace
calls.description: BIEN 2027 is a textile art biennial open call for exhibitors. Selected works will be shown in the biennial taking place in several Slovenian cities, and one selected artist or collective will receive a residency award in Kranj. The call centers on the theme “Traces of Grace.”
calls.project_requirements: Submitted works should be thematically aligned with the central theme, Traces of Grace, and should be primarily created in the medium of textiles or in a medium that references textiles through material, technique, or concept.

calls.title: Open Call: Abstract – Exhibition, Magazine Feature, Artist Interview
calls.description: This open call invites artists to submit work for a virtual exhibition themed around abstraction. Selected artists may also be featured in the magazine and interviewed, with additional promotion through the organisation’s channels. Prizes include a solo show for first prize and a spot in a future group exhibition for second prize.
calls.project_requirements: The Goddessarts Magazine is excited to announce our upcoming theme: Abstract – a celebration of form, color, movement, and emotion. This exhibition invites artists to explore abstraction in all its powerful forms: gestural brushstrokes, geometric clarity, texture-driven work, conceptual abstraction, emotional expression, and beyond. Whether rooted in chaos or calm, minimalism or maximalism, we want to see how abstraction flows through your creative practice. All mediums and styles except video are welcome & everyone is encouraged to apply.

calls.title: OPEN CALL FOR PROJECTS LAB 4 WEIRD FUTURES
calls.description: Medialab Matadero is seeking proposals for the Collaborative Prototyping Lab, a creative residency within the year-long LAB 4 Weird Futures programme. Selected projects will be developed collaboratively during an intensive two-week lab in Madrid with mentors and collaborators, and presented at the OpenLAB festival.
calls.project_requirements: The primary activity of each LAB consists of a Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory: an intensive two-week Laboratory to collaboratively develop 5 experimental projects related to the themes that the LAB 4 addresses. Proposals submitted to this call must necessarily be open to the participation of collaborators interested in participating in their development. The Collaborative Prototyping Laboratory will take place from Monday to Friday between November 12th and 26th, 2025, both included, at Medialab's facilities in Matadero Madrid. The public presentation of the developed projects will be between November 27th and 29th, 2025, at the OpenLAB public event. Participation in the lab sessions must be in person and for the entire duration of the programme.

calls.title: EFFEA Call #5
calls.description: EFFEA Call #5 invites festivals and artists to apply for a residency programme. It supports collaborations between lead and partner festivals and an emerging artist, with the application requiring a proposed residency setup, motivation, and budget information.

calls.title: Seeking Support
calls.description: DGARTES presents open funding opportunities for artistic activity through its support programmes and funding lines. The page points applicants to the candidate support area and the management platform where application forms are available. It also links to the annual declaration listing the open calls and funding amounts for 2026.

calls.title: Artist Project
calls.description: The Artist Project grant supports visual artists who want to realise a concrete artistic plan within a defined working period. It can cover project costs for new work, collaboration, travel, research, mentoring, or a residency in the Netherlands or abroad. The grant is intended to help artists develop work that can strengthen the quality and visibility of contemporary visual art.
calls.project_requirements: To implement a specific plan, tied to a clear working period. It can also involve collaboration. The grant is to help cover project costs, such as the execution of a concrete plan for new work, a collaboration, a period of travel or a working period. It may also entail research, mentoring or a stay at a residency in the Netherlands or abroad. The duration of the contribution must be justified by a global timeline, included in your plan. Applicants are obliged to contribute at least 10% of the total sum being requested from the Mondriaan Fund. This can be in the form of a personal investment, contributions from third parties, an interest-free loan from Fonds Kwadraat or a contribution raised through crowdfunding. This means that the contribution from the Mondriaan Fund will be for a maximum of 90% of the costs that are eligible for the grant. If the application involves another party, such as an art venue, museum, gallery, company or client, the financial contribution from this party must be in acceptable proportion to the contribution requested from the Mondriaan Fund. Cultural institutions are expected to subscribe to the Fair Practice Code. Compliance with the Fair Practice Code automatically means that the institution implements the Guideline for Artists’ Fees. What is eligible: The cost of materials specifically related to the project. Rental of equipment and materials. If equipment is purchased that is strictly necessary for the project, the depreciation costs can be included in the budget. Travel expenses for a return flight, train journey or mileage allowance to and from the main location as stated in the application. Local travel expenses are part of the contribution covering time investment. Hiring third parties (including travel and accommodation expenses, if applicable). Residency expenses: Please note that the contribution covering time investment is halved if a residency fee is included in the budget, or if it becomes apparent that the residency covers the following expenses: accommodation and meals. In the case of an artist’s book, the contribution may only be used for a special publication that can be considered an autonomous work of art in its own right and is produced in an edition of no more than 3 copies. The Artist Project grant may not be used for other publications, but the Publication grant is available for such projects. What is not eligible: Regular expenses, such as ongoing housing costs and child care are not eligible for a grant. The grant is not intended for work for an organisation, for regular work activities, exhibition costs or other costs of presenting work. The grant cannot be used to put previously produced work back into production, to frame work or transfer it to a different medium. Costs associated with a stay abroad and that are covered by the contribution for time investment include accommodation, meals and local travel expenses. An application can be made for these costs for third parties involved with the project. The Artist Project grant may not be used for a working period in a guest studio in the Netherlands or abroad if this studio is offered in the Mondriaan Fund’s Residency The Artist Project grant may not be used for activities or a project at institutions/art venues receiving long-term financial support from one of the Rijkscultuurfondsen (public cultural funds) or the Basic Cultural Infrastructure (BIS), unless it concerns non-standard programming.

calls.title: Craft and design projects in Denmark and abroad
calls.description: This funding programme supports projects for and with Danish craft and design in Denmark and abroad. It can support exhibitions, dissemination, residencies, exchange/work stays, production of works, and other project formats within the craft and design field. The programme also includes support for fees and, in some cases, exhibition remuneration.
calls.project_requirements:
You cannot receive funding for:
• Activities completed before the application deadline
• Courses of study/training courses
• Projects that the committee have previously supported
• Capital investments and operating expenses
• Expenses from previous calendar years. That is, only expenses from either the same or upcoming calendar year can be entered into the budget

What is a project? A project is characterised by having an intention; a project has a time limitation and has a target group. This means that you must be able to define your project with a goal, an intention, a schedule, a budget, a target group or audience and any partners.

The committee wants to award grants to projects that are characterised by good and original ideas, are realistic, achievable and, not least, that create meaning for relevant target groups.

The Committee funds projects of high artistic quality throughout the entire craft and design field and is aware that craft and design is a broad practise. The Committee looks for projects that demonstrate aesthetic potential and a keen understanding of the craft, its materials and sensuousness, as well as projects centered on specific design solutions to specific problems or projects of a more intangible nature.

calls.title: Art and cultural research – thematic call – Artistic and cultural practices among immigrants to Norway 1970–2000
calls.description: This is a thematic funding call for research projects about artistic and cultural practices among immigrants to Norway from 1970 to 2000. It supports projects that document these practices, reflect on how they can be preserved, and examine their traces in today’s art and cultural life in Norway.
calls.project_requirements: The Arts Council announces grants for research projects that document and strengthen knowledge about artistic and cultural practices among immigrants to Norway in the period 1970–2000, that contribute to reflection on how the practices can be documented and preserved, and that examine what traces they have left in today’s art and cultural life in Norway.

calls.title: Residencies / Biodesign Research Residency / BIZIRIK / EKHŌ / BILME
calls.description: The Basque Biodesign Center offers several research residencies focused on biodesign, biofashion, and textile innovation. Residents get access to specialized labs, machinery, technical and teaching support, and a collaborative environment to develop concepts, prototypes, and sustainable materials. The program connects design, technology, craft, and local resources, with residencies aimed at emerging creators as well as experienced textile practitioners.
calls.project_requirements:
Design and innovation for the development of new uses with local waste will be the axis of the project. The main goal of biodesign research residency is to develop new sustainable products, new materials as a way to transform, revaluate and unite rural and urban lifestyles using local raw materials.

The main goal of this residency is to empower experienced professionals to push the boundaries of digital jacquard design in order to develop new sustainable textile structures and alternatives. We seek to transform the fashion industry by bridging cutting-edge technology with the use of novel materials, upcycling local resources, and connecting artisanal heritage with the design of the future.

calls.title: Kunsthaus am Wald International Artist in Residence Program Weitenhagen/ Germany
calls.description: This is an artist-in-residence program for the 2027 season at Kunsthaus am Wald in Weitenhagen, Germany. It invites artists from different disciplines and asks applicants to propose a project for the residency period and present their previous work. The location is remote, and site-specific projects are welcome but not required.
calls.project_requirements: Site-specific projects that engage with the spatial context are welcome, though they are not a mandatory requirement for a residency stay.
